version_notes: v0.3 (unified): Immune City Layer 1 + Mechanism Layer 2 + base44 KG v0.2 merged; gap audit applied.
purpose: Causal knowledge graph of immunological mechanisms from molecular trigger to clinical discovery. Foundation for interactive atlas, causal path explorer, perturbation simulator, evidence engine, and clinical AI reasoning.

nodes.name: Neutrophil
nodes.description: Rapid antimicrobial effector; recruitment and phagocytosis
nodes.clinical_relevance: CGD (NADPH oxidase deficiency → catalase-positive infections); ANCA vasculitis (NETs + FcγRIII activation → necrotising vessel wall destruction); SLE low-density granulocytes (LDG) NETosis drives pDC IFN-α loop

nodes.name: Monocyte
nodes.description: Circulating myeloid cell that can enter tissues and differentiate.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Monocyte-derived macrophages are dominant IL-6 producers in CAR-T CRS (not T cells, explains why tocilizumab not steroids is first-line); CSF-1R on monocyte-derived macrophages = target of axatilimab (cGVHD FDA 2024)

nodes.name: Macrophage
nodes.description: Tissue phagocyte with context-dependent inflammatory, antimicrobial and repair states.
nodes.clinical_relevance: TNF/IL-6/IL-1β production drives RA synovitis; macrophage IL-6 drives COVID-19 ARDS mortality (RECOVERY: dexamethasone benefit only in oxygen-requiring patients); M2/TAM drives cold tumour immune exclusion; FOLR2+ macrophage = universal cold tumour gatekeeper (Nature 2024 AI discovery). R4RA trial: AI pathotyping resolves RA synovium into lymphoid/myeloid/fibroid pathotypes predicting rituximab vs tocilizumab response

nodes.name: Conventional dendritic cell
nodes.description: Professional antigen-presenting cell that efficiently primes naive T cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: cDC1 cross-presents tumour neoantigens to CD8 CTL (requires cGAS-STING activation); absent cDC recruitment = cold tumour (WNT/β-catenin suppresses CCL4→DC axis); STING agonists (diABZI) force cDC maturation; adjuvants force DC maturation (AS01B → TLR4+NLRP3 → Shingrix 91% efficacy ≥70y)

nodes.name: Plasmacytoid dendritic cell
nodes.description: Specialized innate cell capable of strong type-I interferon production.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Produces 1000× more IFN-α per cell than other cells; NET DNA/LL-37 complexes → TLR7/9 → massive IFN-α → SLE interferon signature (75% of patients); drives BAFF production from monocytes; downstream target: anifrolumab (anti-IFNAR1 FDA 2021 SLE)

nodes.name: Natural killer cell
nodes.description: Cytotoxic lymphocyte responding to infected or stressed cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Primary ADCC mechanism of all IgG1 mAbs (rituximab, trastuzumab, obinutuzumab) via FcγRIIIa; afucosylation enhances NK ADCC 50-100× (obinutuzumab LN FDA 2025, benralizumab); anti-NKG2A (monalizumab) releases NK inhibitory checkpoint; MHC-I loss activates NK (missing-self, explains why CAR-NK works when MHC-I is downregulated); SLC6A4 on NK cells suppresses anti-tumour cytotoxicity (AI discovery → fluoxetine+pembrolizumab Phase 2 NSCLC 2024)

nodes.name: Mast cell
nodes.description: Tissue-resident mediator-releasing cell important in allergy and host defence.
nodes.clinical_relevance: FcεRI constitutively loaded with IgE → allergen crosslinks 2+ FcεRI → seconds: histamine, tryptase; minutes: PGD2, LTC4/D4/E4 (1000× more potent bronchoconstrictors than histamine); omalizumab (anti-IgE → FcεRI downregulation); avapritinib (KIT D816V → systemic mastocytosis ORR 75% FDA 2023)

nodes.name: Eosinophil
nodes.description: Granulocyte important in helminth defence and allergic inflammation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-5 survival signal; EGPA, severe eosinophilic asthma, HES; mepolizumab (anti-IL-5, MENSA: exacerbation -53%); benralizumab (anti-IL-5Rα afucosylated → rapid eosinophil depletion within days; every 8 weeks after 3 loading doses)

nodes.name: ILC2
nodes.description: Innate lymphoid cell producing type-2 cytokines at barrier tissues.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Responds to TSLP/IL-25/IL-33 without antigen-specific receptor; drives type-2 asthma even without Th2 cells (explains why IL-5 blockade fails in non-Th2 asthma); target of tezepelumab (anti-TSLP → broadest asthma efficacy NAVIGATOR: 56% exacerbation reduction across ALL endotypes including low-eosinophil)

nodes.name: Naive CD4 T cell
nodes.description: Antigen-specific helper T-cell precursor.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Receives Signal 1 (TCR-pMHC) + Signal 2 (CD28-B7) + Signal 3 (cytokine context) → subset fate; Signal 1 without Signal 2 → anergy (peripheral tolerance mechanism); abatacept (CTLA-4-Ig) blocks Signal 2 → T cell anergy in RA (observational data suggest better response in anti-CCP+ RA)

nodes.name: Th1 cell
nodes.description: Cell-mediated immunity; associated with IFN-γ production.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IFN-γ → macrophage M1 activation → intracellular pathogen killing; drives RA synovitis, T1DM insulitis (nPOD dominant cell), MS CNS inflammation; teplizumab (anti-CD3 Fc-silent) shifts Th1:Treg ratio in T1DM islets → TN10 trial: 25-month T1DM onset delay (FDA 2022, first autoimmune prevention drug)

nodes.name: Th2 cell
nodes.description: Type-2 immunity; associated with IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-4 → IgE class switching; IL-5 → eosinophil activation; IL-13 → mucus/bronchoconstriction; helminth expulsion in normal biology; misdirected at harmless allergens in atopy; dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα: blocks IL-4 and IL-13 simultaneously via shared Type II receptor, mechanistic basis of its breadth across AD, asthma, CRSwNP, EoE)

nodes.name: Th17 cell
nodes.description: Barrier defence and inflammatory responses; supports neutrophil-associated immunity.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-17A → neutrophil recruitment, keratinocyte hyperproliferation; AS entheseal inflammation; IBD mucosal; RORγt master TF; maintained by IL-23 (not IL-6+TGF-β which generates Th17, IL-23 renews them); absolute contraindication: anti-IL-17A worsens active IBD (IL-17A essential for gut epithelial tight junctions)

nodes.name: Treg cell
nodes.description: Regulatory T cell supporting peripheral immune tolerance and suppression.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IPEX (Foxp3 mutation) → catastrophic multiorgan autoimmunity: proves Tregs essential for preventing autoimmunity. Suppresses via IL-10/TGF-β/CTLA-4 (B7 trans-endocytosis)/CD39→adenosine. Low-dose IL-2 (1-3M IU SC) expands Tregs preferentially (highest CD25 = highest sensitivity); CAR-Treg LIBERATE Phase 1 (HLA-A2-specific, renal transplant 2024); ONE Study: polyclonal Treg infusion → 0 rejection episodes at 4yr vs 21.1% controls

nodes.name: CD8 cytotoxic T lymphocyte
nodes.description: Kills antigen-bearing target cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Kills via perforin/granzyme B (MHC-I restricted; CAR-T bypasses this requirement). Exhaustion states: progenitor exhausted (TCF-1+/PD-1+/TIM-3-) → responds to anti-PD-1 (KEYnote-006: 5yr OS 38.7%). Terminal exhausted (TOX+/TCF-1-/TIM-3+) → does not respond. TEMRA (CD45RA+/CD57+/CD28-) dominates elderly → no anti-PD-1 benefit. Anti-PD-1 mechanism: rescues progenitor exhausted CTLs

nodes.name: Tfh cell
nodes.description: Provides B-cell help in follicles and germinal centres.
nodes.clinical_relevance: GC B cell help → SHM → affinity maturation → class switching → high-affinity IgG; circulating Tfh (cTfh: CXCR5+PD-1+CD4+) correlates with SLE disease activity and independently predicts LN flares; autoreactive GC driven by Tfh in SLE → anti-dsDNA IgG production

nodes.name: B cell
nodes.description: Antigen-recognizing lymphocyte that can differentiate into antibody-secreting cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: V(D)J recombination → 10^12 BCR diversity; GC → AID-driven SHM + class switching; produces ANCA (vasculitis), ACPA (RA), anti-dsDNA (SLE), OCBs (MS); CD20+ → depleted by rituximab/ocrelizumab BUT plasma cells are CD20-negative and missed

nodes.name: Plasma cell
nodes.description: Specialized antibody-secreting cell.
nodes.clinical_relevance: CD20-negative: missed by all anti-CD20 drugs. CD19+ plasmablasts reached by inebilizumab (MITIGATE: IgG4-RD 87% flare reduction). BCMA+ long-lived plasma cells targeted by CAR-T (cilta-cel CARTITUDE-4: PFS HR 0.26); teclistamab (anti-BCMA×CD3 bispecific). In autoimmunity: SLE anti-dsDNA-producing plasma cells persist after rituximab → driving ongoing LN

nodes.name: Memory B cell
nodes.description: Long-lived B-cell population supporting rapid secondary responses.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Class-switched, high-affinity BCR; basis of vaccination memory; rapid recall in 3-5 days vs 10-14 days primary response; depleted by anti-CD20; reconstitutes autoreactive pool after rituximab withdrawal (explains SLE relapse after rituximab)

nodes.name: Follicular dendritic cell
nodes.description: Germinal-centre stromal cell that displays native antigen to B cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Displays native antigen in GC → positive selection of highest-affinity B cells (Darwinian selection within lymph node); drives autoreactive B cell affinity maturation in SLE; interlocks with Tfh-B cell collaboration

nodes.name: TNF
nodes.description: Pro-inflammatory cytokine with major roles in tissue inflammation and granuloma biology.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Granuloma maintenance (anti-TNF → TB/fungal reactivation, mandatory LTBI screening before anti-TNF); TNFR2 cardioprotective on cardiomyocytes (anti-TNF absoluteLY contraindicated in CHF NYHA III-IV); membrane TNF → reverse signalling → macrophage/T cell apoptosis (infliximab/adalimumab fistula healing in CD; etanercept cannot bind membrane TNF → no reverse signalling → no fistula healing)

nodes.name: IL-1β
nodes.description: Inflammatory cytokine involved in fever and local inflammatory responses.
nodes.clinical_relevance: NLRP3 caspase-1 cleaves pro-IL-1β → active form; gout (uric acid crystals → NLRP3 → IL-1β → acute joint inflammation → colchicine/canakinumab); CANTOS trial (N=10,061): canakinumab MACE -15% HR 0.85, LDL unchanged → first clinical proof macrophage NLRP3-IL-1β causally drives CVD; lung cancer -77% unexpected finding

nodes.name: IL-6
nodes.description: Cytokine involved in inflammation, acute-phase responses and B-cell/plasma-cell biology.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-6R → JAK1/TYK2 → STAT3 → acute phase (CRP, fibrinogen), Th17 differentiation (with TGF-β), osteoclast activation, T cell exhaustion in TME; clinical safety: anti-IL-6R suppresses CRP production → patients can have severe infection with NO fever or elevated CRP, patient education mandatory; lipid monitoring at 4-8 weeks (LDL rises)

nodes.name: IL-12
nodes.description: Promotes Th1/NK-associated IFN-γ responses.
nodes.clinical_relevance: DC-produced Th1 polarising cytokine (IL-12 → IL-12R → JAK2/TYK2 → STAT4 → T-bet → IFN-γ); shared p40 subunit with IL-23 → both blocked by ustekinumab; IL-12 deficiency → susceptibility to non-tuberculous mycobacteria; anti-IL-23 p19 inhibitors (risankizumab) spare IL-12 → preserve Th1/antimycobacterial immunity

nodes.name: IL-23
nodes.description: Supports effector/pathogenic Th17 biology in multiple inflammatory settings.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Th17 maintenance/RENEWAL (not just generation, IL-6+TGF-β generates Th17; IL-23 maintains/renews them → anti-IL-23 has superior durability vs anti-IL-17A); SEQUENCE trial (2023): risankizumab vs ustekinumab in CD → 45% vs 33% remission. Anti-IL-23 p19 inhibitors spare IL-12 (shared p40 subunit in ustekinumab)

nodes.name: IFN-γ
nodes.description: Th1/NK cytokine that activates macrophage antimicrobial programmes.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Macrophage M1 activation → iNOS → NO → intracellular killing (TB defence); drives Th1 disease; adaptive immune resistance in cancer: TIL IFN-γ → JAK1/2 → STAT1 → PD-L1 upregulation on tumour (the tumour upregulates PD-L1 in response to the very T cells attacking it)

nodes.name: IL-4
nodes.description: Type-2 cytokine involved in Th2 differentiation and B-cell class-switching contexts.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IgE class switching; Th2 differentiation; IL-4Rα/γc (Type I receptor, haematopoietic cells) OR IL-4Rα/IL-13Rα1 (Type II receptor, non-haematopoietic, also binds IL-13); dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα) blocks both IL-4 and IL-13 simultaneously via shared Type II receptor

nodes.name: IL-5
nodes.description: Promotes eosinophil growth, recruitment and activation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Eosinophil growth, differentiation, activation, survival; target of mepolizumab (anti-IL-5; MENSA: exacerbation -53% in severe eosinophilic asthma) and reslizumab (anti-IL-5); EGPA (eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis), HES, severe asthma

nodes.name: IL-13
nodes.description: Type-2 cytokine associated with mucus production, tissue responses and fibrosis-associated biology.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Goblet cell hyperplasia (mucus overproduction); smooth muscle hyperresponsiveness; FLG (filaggrin) downregulation (→ atopic march: skin sensitisation → food allergy → rhinitis → asthma); eotaxin production (eosinophil recruitment); blocked by dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα Type II receptor)

nodes.name: IL-17A
nodes.description: Barrier inflammatory cytokine that supports neutrophil-associated host defence.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-17RA+IL-17RC → NF-κB+MAPK → CXCL8 (neutrophil chemokine), antimicrobial peptides, keratinocyte hyperproliferation; gut barrier tight junction maintenance; Absolute contraindication: active IBD (blockade → tight junction loss → bacterial translocation → IBD flare). Antifungal mucosal defence → Candida susceptibility with IL-17A blockade

nodes.name: IL-10
nodes.description: Immune-regulatory cytokine that limits inflammatory responses in many contexts.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Master anti-inflammatory; Treg effector cytokine; limits inflammatory overshoot; macrophage deactivation; B cell survival; therapeutic IL-10 (trials in IBD failed due to systemic immunosuppression at required doses)

nodes.name: TGF-β
nodes.description: Context-dependent regulatory cytokine involved in Treg biology and tissue remodelling.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Treg induction (with IL-2 → Foxp3 stabilisation); Th17 generation (with IL-6); fibrosis (cGVHD FAP+ fibroblast activation; IPF); SMAD2/3 pathway; TNIK (Traf2-NCK Interacting Kinase) identified by PandaOmics AI as IPF driver → rentosertib (INS018_055) Phase 2a positive (Nature Medicine 2025: +98.4mL FVC vs -62.3mL placebo)

nodes.name: CXCL8 / IL-8
nodes.description: Chemokine strongly associated with neutrophil chemoattraction.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Primary neutrophil chemotactic gradient; CXCR2 receptor on neutrophils; drives neutrophil transmigration in ANCA vasculitis, psoriatic skin, IBD; CXCR2 antagonists in COPD Phase 2

nodes.name: CXCL10
nodes.description: Chemokine associated with interferon-driven recruitment of CXCR3-positive cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IFN-γ-driven chemokine (CXCR3+ T cells); elevated in SLE alongside IFN-I signature; severe COVID-19 hyperinflammation marker; also elevated in IBD, hepatitis C-associated fibrosis

nodes.name: GM-CSF
nodes.description: Myeloid differentiation and inflammatory activation factor.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Myeloid differentiation and activation; elevated in RA synovium; target of otilimab (anti-GM-CSF, Phase 3 RA); therapeutic G-CSF (filgrastim/lenograstim) mobilises HSCs from bone marrow for HSCT collection

nodes.name: TLR4
nodes.description: Recognizes bacterial lipopolysaccharide in cooperation with accessory molecules.
nodes.clinical_relevance: LPS sensor (with MD-2+CD14 co-receptors) → MyD88→IRAK4→TRAF6→NF-κB AND TRIF→TBK1→IRF3→IFN-β; most clinically relevant TLR in sepsis (LPS-driven systemic inflammation); gut TLR4 constitutively suppressed to tolerate commensal LPS

nodes.name: TLR3
nodes.description: Endosomal sensor for double-stranded RNA.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Endosomal dsRNA sensor (viral replication intermediates); TRIF→IRF3→IFN-β (MyD88-independent); TLR3 agonist polyI:C → vaccine adjuvant; TLR3 deficiency → severe HSV encephalitis

nodes.name: TLR7
nodes.description: Endosomal sensor for single-stranded RNA.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Endosomal ssRNA sensor; pDC TLR7 → IFN-α; SLE pathogenesis: NET DNA/RNA complexes → TLR7/9 → massive IFN-α → interferon signature; HCQ alkalinises endosomes → TLR7/9 blockade → reduces pDC IFN-α (mechanism of HCQ in SLE)

nodes.name: NLRP3
nodes.description: Inflammasome sensor responding to diverse cellular danger signals.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Danger sensor for uric acid crystals/cholesterol crystals/silica/ATP/K+ efflux; activates NLRP3 inflammasome complex → IL-1β + pyroptosis; CAPS (gain-of-function mutations); gout; atherosclerosis

nodes.name: TNFR1
nodes.description: TNF receptor capable of inflammatory and cell-death signalling.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Ubiquitous expression; death domain → apoptosis; TRADD→TRAF2→NF-κB (survival); drives pro-inflammatory signalling; dominant receptor for soluble TNF; target of anti-TNF therapy (blocks TNFR1 engagement)

nodes.name: TNFR2
nodes.description: TNF receptor with strong context dependence in immune regulation and tissue responses.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Immune cell expression + CARDIOMYOCYTES; no death domain; TRAF2→NF-κB → survival/proliferation of Tregs; cardioprotective via TNFR2 → absolute contraindication for anti-TNF in CHF NYHA III-IV (TNFR2 cardioprotection abolished); prefers membrane-bound TNF → etanercept (TNFR2-Fc decoy) cannot engage membrane TNF → lower TNFR2 activity change

nodes.name: IL-6R
nodes.description: Receptor component mediating IL-6 signalling.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-6Rα (soluble + membrane) + gp130 (ubiquitous signal transducer) → JAK1/TYK2 → STAT3; tocilizumab (anti-IL-6Rα, binds soluble+membrane) vs sarilumab (anti-IL-6Rα different epitope) vs siltuximab (anti-IL-6 itself, not receptor)

nodes.name: IL-12 receptor
nodes.description: Receptor complex mediating IL-12 signalling.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-12Rβ1+IL-12Rβ2 → JAK2/TYK2 → STAT4 → T-bet; shared IL-12Rβ1 with IL-23R → ustekinumab (anti-p40) blocks both IL-12 and IL-23 signalling; IL-12Rβ1 or IL-12Rβ2 deficiency → susceptibility to NTM and Salmonella

nodes.name: IL-23R
nodes.description: Receptor component mediating IL-23 signalling.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-23R+IL-12Rβ1 → JAK2/TYK2 → STAT3 → RORγt stabilisation (Th17 renewal); IL-23R variants associate with IBD, AS, psoriasis (GWAS); guselkumab, risankizumab (anti-IL-23 p19) block IL-23 before receptor engagement

nodes.name: IL-17RA
nodes.description: Core receptor component for IL-17A signalling.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-17RA+IL-17RC (forms active receptor complex for IL-17A and IL-17F) → Act1 adaptor → TRAF6 → NF-κB+MAPK → CXCL8, antimicrobial peptides, MMPs; gut barrier tight junction proteins (claudins, occludins) maintained by IL-17A signalling → worsens IBD when blocked

nodes.name: NF-κB signalling
nodes.description: Central transcriptional inflammatory pathway downstream of many innate receptors.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Downstream of TLRs (MyD88→IRAK4→TRAF6→IKK→IκB phosphorylation→NF-κB nuclear), TNFR1, IL-1R, BCR, TCR; drives TNF, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-8, IL-12, COX-2, VCAM-1, E-selectin gene transcription; suppressed by glucocorticoids (broad NF-κB suppression = mechanism of steroid anti-inflammatory effect)

nodes.name: JAK-STAT signalling
nodes.description: Core intracellular signalling route used by many cytokine receptors.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Downstream of most cytokine receptors (IL-6R→JAK1/TYK2→STAT3; IL-4R→JAK1/JAK3→STAT6; IFN-αβR→JAK1/TYK2→STAT1/2; IL-2R→JAK1/JAK3→STAT5); JAK1/2/3 inhibitors (baricitinib/tofacitinib/upadacitinib) approved across RA, AD, IBD, alopecia, COVID-19; FDA 2021 boxed warning for JAK inhibitors (MACE/VTE/malignancy) in patients ≥50y with ≥1 CV risk factor; deucravacitinib (allosteric TYK2 JH2 domain) selectively blocks IL-12/IL-23/IFN-I, no JAK class boxed warning

nodes.name: NLRP3 inflammasome
nodes.description: Inflammasome pathway supporting maturation of IL-1β and IL-18.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Activated by uric acid crystals (gout), cholesterol crystals (atherosclerosis), silica (occupational autoimmunity), ATP, K+ efflux; NLRP3+ASC+caspase-1 → IL-1β+IL-18+pyroptosis; colchicine (blocks NLRP3 assembly + NETs; COLCOT: MACE -23%; LoDoCo-2: MACE -31%); MCC950/dapansutrile (direct NLRP3 inhibitors Phase 2); CAPS (NLRP3 gain-of-function → autoinflammatory disease)

nodes.name: Type-I interferon signalling
nodes.description: IFN-I pathway leading to interferon-stimulated gene expression.
nodes.clinical_relevance: cGAS-STING→TBK1→IRF3→IFN-β; TLR7/9→IRF7→IFN-α (pDC dominant); IFNAR1/2→JAK1/TYK2→STAT1/2+IRF9→ISGF3→ISGs (IFIT1, MX1, OAS1); SLE: 75% of patients IFN-signature-high → anifrolumab (anti-IFNAR1) FDA 2021; ISG15+ macrophage exclusive to Class III/IV LN (AI discovery → explains anifrolumab mechanism in proliferative LN)

nodes.name: Antigen presentation via MHC-II
nodes.description: Peptide-MHC-II presentation to CD4 T cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: APC-restricted; CD4+ T cell activation; peptide 13-25aa loaded in endosome; HLA polymorphism determines which self-peptides are presented → autoimmune disease susceptibility (HLA-DRB1*15:01 → MS 6×; HLA-DRB1 SE → seropositive RA; HLA-DQ2/DQ8 → T1DM)

nodes.name: Antigen presentation via MHC-I
nodes.description: Peptide-MHC-I presentation to CD8 T cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: All nucleated cells; CD8+ CTL activation (8-10aa peptide); MHC-I downregulation = dominant cancer immune escape (B2M mutation, NLRC5 silencing, JAK1/2 loss) → CD8 CTL blinded; CAR-T bypasses MHC-I restriction (explains CAR-T activity where ICI fails)

nodes.name: T-cell receptor signalling
nodes.description: Signal integration downstream of TCR engagement.
nodes.clinical_relevance: TCR+pMHC → ZAP-70 → LAT → PLCγ → Ca2+/PKCθ → NFAT/NF-κB/AP-1 → IL-2/CD25/CD69; PD-1→SHP-2 dephosphorylates ZAP-70 → T cell inactivation (anti-PD-1 restores ZAP-70 phosphorylation)

nodes.name: Germinal-centre reaction
nodes.description: B-cell selection, class switching and affinity maturation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: AID-driven SHM (affinity maturation) + class switching; Darwinian selection by FDC + Tfh signals; produces high-affinity IgG plasma cells + memory B cells; also generates oncogenic translocations (BCL2 t(14;18)→follicular lymphoma; MYC t(8;14)→Burkitt lymphoma)

nodes.name: Th1 differentiation
nodes.description: Differentiation programme associated with IL-12/STAT4/T-bet biology.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-12→IL-12R→JAK2/TYK2→STAT4→T-bet → IFN-γ production; drives intracellular pathogen immunity (TB) and autoimmune Th1 disease (RA, T1DM, MS)

nodes.name: Th17 differentiation
nodes.description: Differentiation programme involving IL-6/TGF-β and IL-23 support.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IL-6+TGF-β→RORγt (generation); IL-23→IL-23R→STAT3→RORγt stabilisation (maintenance/renewal, the therapeutic difference between anti-IL-17A and anti-IL-23 durability profiles); drives psoriasis, AS, IBD mucosal inflammation

nodes.name: Skin
nodes.description: Barrier tissue with resident immune sentinels.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Epicutaneous sensitisation (FLG mutation → skin barrier defect → pollen/peanut/mite sensitisation through skin → IgE → systemic allergy); LL-37+dsDNA NET complexes in psoriatic skin → pDC TLR9 → IFN-α → DC maturation → Th17 amplification; target of dupilumab (AD), secukinumab (psoriasis)

nodes.name: Lung
nodes.description: Respiratory tissue with extensive innate and adaptive immunity.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Alveolar macrophage (resident, anti-inflammatory in health); COVID-19 ARDS: alveolar macrophage → IL-6 storm → RECOVERY dexamethasone benefit; IPF: M2 alveolar macrophage+fibroblast activation; TRM in lung → intranasal vaccine required for mucosal protection; CRS: pulmonary oedema from capillary leak

nodes.name: Gut mucosa
nodes.description: Microbiota-rich barrier immune compartment.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT) houses 70% of immune system; F. prausnitzii → butyrate → Foxp3 Treg induction; gut dysbiosis → reduced Treg induction → lower tolerance threshold; antibiotics within 30 days of ICI → reduced microbiome diversity → shorter PFS/OS (Routy Science 2018); IL-17A maintains gut epithelial tight junctions → blockade worsens IBD

nodes.name: Lymph node
nodes.description: Site of antigen presentation and lymphocyte activation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Antigen presentation hub: DC migrates from tissue to lymph node paracortex → encounters naive T cell (1/10^4-6 frequency); immunological synapse formation; GC in cortical follicles → B cell affinity maturation; without lymph nodes (surgical dissection, genetic asplenia) → severely impaired T cell priming

nodes.name: Blood
nodes.description: Transport compartment for immune cells and soluble mediators.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Transport compartment; biologic drug distribution; drug trough level monitoring (infliximab TDM); circulating Tfh (cTfh) correlates with SLE disease activity; TEMRA cells dominant in elderly blood; anti-drug antibody (ADA) formation detected in blood; HCQ blood level monitoring in SLE

nodes.name: Synovium
nodes.description: Joint tissue central to rheumatoid arthritis pathology.
nodes.clinical_relevance: RA pathological focus: CD68+ macrophage density in synovial lining layer correlates with DAS28; FLS (fibroblast-like synoviocytes) invasion + pannus + RANKL-osteoclast → joint erosion; R4RA AI pathotyping: lymphoid/myeloid/fibroid synovial pathotypes predict biologic response

nodes.name: Tumour microenvironment
nodes.description: Local ecosystem of malignant, immune and stromal cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Immunosuppressive milieu: Tregs (CCL2/5/22 recruited), MDSCs (arginase-1, iNOS), M2 TAMs (IL-10/TGF-β/VEGF), adenosine (CD39+CD73), IDO (tryptophan depletion → kynurenine → Treg induction); cold tumour = absent TIL (WNT/β-catenin → no DC recruitment); STING agonists (diABZI) 'heat' cold tumours; FOLR2+ macrophage = universal TME gatekeeper (AI discovery Nature 2024)

nodes.name: Granuloma
nodes.description: Organized inflammatory structure important for containment of some persistent pathogens.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Organised immune structure containing intracellular pathogens (TB, fungal, Nocardia); TNF essential for granuloma integrity (anti-TNF → granuloma dissolution → TB reactivation → mandatory LTBI screening before anti-TNF); sarcoidosis: non-caseating granuloma without identified organism

nodes.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
nodes.description: Chronic inflammatory arthritis involving TNF, IL-6 and other inflammatory pathways.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Dominant drivers: CD4+ Th1/Th17 synovitis + ACPA-producing GC B cells + synovial macrophage M1 (TNF/IL-6/RANKL); HLA-DRB1 SE → citrullinated protein presentation; ACPA+ RA may respond better to abatacept (observational data); R4RA AI pathotyping → rituximab (lymphoid) vs tocilizumab (myeloid)

nodes.name: Multiple sclerosis
nodes.description: Immune-mediated CNS disease involving inflammatory and adaptive immune mechanisms.
nodes.clinical_relevance: RRMS: CD4+ Th1/Th17 breach BBB (VLA-4/VCAM-1 → natalizumab); Progressive: B cell leptomeningeal aggregates drive compartmentalised CNS inflammation (ORATORIO: ocrelizumab → first positive PPMS trial; proves B cells not T cells drive PPMS); EBV causal factor (Bjornevik Science 2022: 32× risk increase, 5yr lag → EBV vaccine Phase 1 for MS prevention 2025)

nodes.name: Psoriasis
nodes.description: Chronic inflammatory skin disease with important IL-23/IL-17-axis biology.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Th17/ILC3 → IL-17A → keratinocyte hyperproliferation; pDC LL-37/DNA complex → TLR9 → IFN-α → DC → Th17 amplification; HLA-Cw*06 (45-67% of patients, predicts ustekinumab response); IL-23 p19 inhibitors show superior PASI 90 durability (>70% at 5yr) vs IL-17A inhibitors; bimekizumab (anti-IL-17A+F dual) highest PASI 100 rates (67% at week 16)

nodes.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
nodes.description: Chronic intestinal inflammation including Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Th17/ILC3 → IL-17A mucosal; macrophage IL-6/TNF transmural (CD); SEQUENCE trial (2023): risankizumab vs ustekinumab → 45% vs 33% remission in CD; U-EXCEED: upadacitinib 45mg vs adalimumab → 39% vs 22% remission (first JAK inhibitor superiority over anti-TNF in CD); F. prausnitzii predicts ustekinumab response (AUC 0.84); vedolizumab (gut-selective anti-α4β7)

nodes.name: Asthma
nodes.description: Heterogeneous airway disease; type-2 biology is important in many phenotypes.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Heterogeneous: type-2 (eosinophilic, IL-5/IL-13 driven, responds to dupilumab/mepolizumab) vs non-type-2 (IL-5-low, ILC2-driven); tezepelumab (anti-TSLP) effective across ALL endotypes (NAVIGATOR: 56% exacerbation reduction even in low-eosinophil asthma, endotype-agnostic); asthma + IBD overlap → avoid anti-IL-17A

nodes.name: Atopic dermatitis
nodes.description: Inflammatory skin disease with type-2 biology in many patients.
nodes.clinical_relevance: FLG mutation → skin barrier defect → epicutaneous sensitisation; IL-4/IL-13/IL-31 Th2 axis; atopic march (AD → food allergy → asthma); dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα): SOLO 1/2 EASI-75 38% vs 10%; conjunctivitis SE (10-28%) = IL-4/13 regulate ocular goblet cells → mechanistic prediction; upadacitinib (JAK1) + tralokinumab (anti-IL-13) alternatives

nodes.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
nodes.description: Systemic autoimmune disease with immune-complex and interferon-associated biology.
nodes.clinical_relevance: NET→pDC→IFN-α→BAFF→autoreactive B cell rescue→Tfh→GC→anti-dsDNA→IC deposition→LN. 75% IFN-high → anifrolumab (anti-IFNAR1); APOL1 G1/G2 (African ancestry, 20-25%) → worse LN outcomes; Class III/IV LN: MMF+voclosporin (AURORA: 41% CRR vs 23%) or obinutuzumab+MMF (NOBILITY: 50% vs 30% CRR, FDA 2025); HCQ backbone for ALL SLE patients

nodes.name: Severe combined immunodeficiency
nodes.description: Profound adaptive immune impairment; molecular causes are heterogeneous.
nodes.clinical_relevance: X-SCID (IL2RG/γc → no T/NK); ADA-SCID (dATP accumulation → lymphocyte apoptosis); RAG1/2 (no V(D)J recombination). TREC newborn screening → HSCT before age 3.5 months → >95% OS; Strimvelis (ADA-SCID gene therapy, EMA 2016); WASKYRA/OTL-103 (WAS gene therapy, FDA 2025, first US gene therapy for PID)

nodes.name: Chronic granulomatous disease
nodes.description: Defective phagocyte oxidative burst with susceptibility to recurrent infections.
nodes.clinical_relevance: CYBB/gp91phox (X-linked, 70%); NCF1/p47phox autosomal recessive; DHR flow cytometry diagnostic (no fluorescence shift on PMA stimulation = CGD); susceptibility to catalase-positive organisms only (S. aureus, Aspergillus, Nocardia, Serratia, Burkholderia); SIN-lentiviral gene therapy Phase 2/3, filing expected 2025-2026

nodes.name: Tuberculosis
nodes.description: Mycobacterial infection in which macrophage and granuloma biology are central.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IFN-γ → macrophage activation → intracellular killing essential; TNF maintains granuloma integrity (anti-TNF → granuloma dissolution → reactivation TB, 40× risk with anti-TNF vs general population → mandatory LTBI screening); IL-12 deficiency → disseminated non-tuberculous mycobacteria

nodes.name: Sepsis
nodes.description: Dysregulated host response to infection with organ dysfunction.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Dysregulated host response to infection; macrophage/monocyte → TNF/IL-1β/IL-6 storm → endothelial activation → DIC → MOF; Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundles; anti-TNF failed in sepsis trials (TNF has context-dependent protective roles); IL-6R blockade also failed in bacterial sepsis; different from COVID-19 ARDS where IL-6R blockade works

nodes.name: Melanoma
nodes.description: Malignant melanoma shaped by tumour immune recognition and immune escape.
nodes.clinical_relevance: High TMB (UV-induced mutation burden → many neoantigens → TIL-rich); dominant checkpoint: PD-1 axis; KEYnote-006: pembrolizumab vs ipilimumab → 5yr OS 38.7% vs 31.1%; nivo+ipi (CheckMate-067): 5yr OS 52%; WNT/β-catenin activation in 25-35% → cold tumour → anti-PD-1 non-response; KEYnote-942: mRNA-4157 neoantigen vaccine + pembrolizumab RFS HR 0.561

nodes.name: Infliximab
nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody targeting TNF.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Chimeric IgG1; binds soluble AND membrane TNF → reverse signalling → macrophage/T cell apoptosis in granuloma → fistula healing in CD (etanercept cannot); ATTRACT trial (2000): first biologic to show structural protection in RA; risk: TB reactivation (mandatory LTBI), infusion reactions (slow first infusion), anti-drug antibodies (minimised by concomitant MTX); TDM: trough >3-7 μg/mL for mucosal healing in IBD

nodes.name: Adalimumab
nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody targeting TNF.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Fully human IgG1 SC; binds soluble+membrane TNF; broadest approved indication (RA, PsA, AS, CD/UC, psoriasis, JIA, uveitis, HS); anti-drug antibody (ADA) rate 25-40% (reduced with concomitant MTX); preferred in pregnancy over infliximab (later switch: both cross placenta via FcRn → avoid live vaccines in infant for 6 months); biosimilars available

nodes.name: Tocilizumab
nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody targeting IL-6R.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Humanised anti-IL-6Rα (soluble+membrane); IV+SC; Clinical warning: suppresses CRP production (IL-6R blocked → hepatic CRP synthesis reduced) → fever and CRP cannot monitor for infection in patients on tocilizumab, patient education mandatory; lipid monitoring 4-8 weeks; first-line CRS Grade 2+ (8mg/kg IV); GCA first biologic approval; RA, sJIA, COVID-19 ARDS

nodes.name: Secukinumab
nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody targeting IL-17A.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Fully human IgG1κ (no enhanced ADCC vs ixekizumab IgG4κ); anti-IL-17A; approved: psoriasis, PsA, AS, NR-axSpA; Contraindication: active IBD (IL-17A maintains gut barrier); Candida mucosal infections; ERASURE/FIXTURE Phase 3 (plaque psoriasis); first anti-IL-17A class drug

nodes.name: Ustekinumab
nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody targeting the shared p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Human IgG1κ; anti-p40 (shared subunit of IL-12 and IL-23) → blocks both; quarterly SC maintenance; psoriasis, PsA, CD, UC; SEQUENCE trial: risankizumab (selective anti-IL-23 p19) > ustekinumab in CD; HLA-Cw*06 positive patients may respond better (PSOLAR data); F. prausnitzii abundance predicts response in UC (AUC 0.84)

nodes.name: Dupilumab
nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody blocking IL-4/IL-13 receptor signalling.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Human IgG4κ; anti-IL-4Rα → blocks both IL-4 (Th2 differentiation, IgE class switching) and IL-13 (goblet cells, smooth muscle, FLG suppression) simultaneously via shared Type II receptor subunit; broadest indication of any biologic: AD, severe asthma, CRSwNP, EoE, prurigo nodularis, COPD T2 (FDA 2024); Side effect: conjunctivitis 10-28% in AD (IL-4/13 regulate ocular surface goblet cells → mechanistic prediction, lubricating drops + ophthalmology)

nodes.name: Etanercept
nodes.description: Soluble TNF receptor fusion protein.
nodes.clinical_relevance: TNFR2-Fc decoy protein; binds soluble TNF only (cannot bind membrane-bound TNF → no reverse signalling → does not work in fistulising Crohn's disease); lower TB reactivation risk vs other anti-TNFs (granuloma membrane TNF less affected); does not work in UC or CD (hence no IBD approval); not a monoclonal antibody (no ADCC, no CDC)

nodes.name: Pembrolizumab
nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody targeting PD-1.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Humanised IgG4κ (stabilised to prevent Fab arm exchange); anti-PD-1; rescues progenitor exhausted CD8 CTLs (TCF-1+/PD-1+/TIM-3-); KEYnote-006 (melanoma): 5yr OS 38.7% vs 31.1% ipilimumab; FDA-approved 20+ tumour types; tumour-agnostic: MSI-H/dMMR (2017), TMB-H ≥10 mut/Mb (2020).

nodes.name: Nivolumab
nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody targeting PD-1.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Fully human IgG4κ (stabilised); anti-PD-1; approved: melanoma, NSCLC, SCLC, RCC, HCC, CRC (MSI-H), HNSCC, gastric, esophageal; nivo+ipi (CheckMate-067): melanoma 5yr OS 52%; CheckMate-8HW: nivo+ipi vs chemo in MSI-H mCRC → PFS HR 0.21

nodes.name: Corticosteroid
nodes.description: Drug class that suppresses multiple inflammatory gene programmes.
nodes.clinical_relevance: GR → NF-κB suppression (IκBα induction → sequesters NF-κB) + AP-1 suppression + HDAC recruitment → broad anti-inflammatory; RECOVERY trial: dexamethasone 6mg 10 days → MACE 23% vs 26% in oxygen-requiring COVID-19 (RR 0.64); harm in non-oxygen-requiring (RR 1.19, viral phase); CRS Grade 3-4: methylprednisolone 1-2mg/kg/day IV

nodes.name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
nodes.description: Intracellular pathogen associated with granulomatous inflammation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Intracellular pathogen evading phagolysosomal killing; requires IFN-γ-driven macrophage M1 activation + TNF-driven granuloma containment; TNF essential → anti-TNF → 40× TB reactivation risk → mandatory LTBI screening (IGRA) before ANY biologic; rifampicin enzyme inducer → drug interactions with DMARDs

nodes.name: Influenza A virus
nodes.description: Respiratory virus sensed by innate antiviral pathways.
nodes.clinical_relevance: RIG-I → MAVS → IFN-β; CD8 CTL → perforin/granzyme killing of infected cells; NK cell ADCC; influenza vaccine efficacy reduced in elderly (immunosenescence) and CMV seropositive (40-60% worse response); morning influenza vaccination → 30% higher antibody titre (JCI 2019)

nodes.name: Candida albicans
nodes.description: Opportunistic fungus controlled in part by Th17/neutrophil-associated immunity.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Th17/neutrophil/IL-17A axis responsible for mucosal Candida defence; IL-17A blockade (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab) → Candida mucosal infections; IL-17A deficiency (STAT3 mutation / Job syndrome) → recurrent mucocutaneous candidiasis

nodes.name: Schistosoma species
nodes.description: Helminthic parasite associated with type-2 immune responses.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Drives protective Th2/IgE/mast cell/eosinophil response; hygiene hypothesis: reduced helminth exposure in modern environments → Th2 system misdirected at harmless allergens → allergy epidemic; LEAP trial: early oral peanut introduction 80% allergy reduction (tolerance induction)

nodes.name: SARS-CoV-2
nodes.description: Respiratory coronavirus eliciting innate and adaptive immune responses.
nodes.clinical_relevance: RIG-I/MDA5 + TLR7 → type I IFN antiviral response (early phase); severe disease: monocyte-derived macrophage IL-6 storm → ARDS (cytokine phase); RECOVERY trial: dexamethasone beneficial only in oxygen-requiring (cytokine phase), harmful in non-oxygen-requiring (viral replication phase, immune suppression worsens viral clearance)

nodes.name: C-reactive protein (CRP)
nodes.description: Acute-phase protein used as a systemic inflammation marker.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Acute phase reactant (IL-6-driven hepatic production); rises within 6-8h of inflammatory stimulus; falls rapidly with resolution; clinical TRAP: tocilizumab/sarilumab suppress CRP production (block IL-6R) → CRP cannot be used to monitor infection or inflammation in patients on IL-6R antagonists; hsCRP (high-sensitivity) used in CANTOS (>2mg/L → enrolled; fell with canakinumab confirming anti-IL-1β mechanism)

nodes.name: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR)
nodes.description: Non-specific laboratory measure associated with systemic inflammation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Non-specific; rises with fibrinogen, IgG, IgM (all acute phase reactants); less responsive to treatment change than CRP; used in DAS28-ESR (RA disease activity score); elevated in PMR/GCA → falls with steroid response (diagnostic and monitoring)

nodes.name: Faecal calprotectin
nodes.description: Biomarker used to assess intestinal inflammation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Neutrophil cytoplasmic protein; correlates with intestinal mucosal inflammation; predicts IBD mucosal healing (target <250 μg/g); distinguishes IBD from IBS (elevated in IBD, normal in IBS); F. prausnitzii abundance predicts ustekinumab response in UC (AUC 0.84), connects microbiome to calprotectin response

nodes.name: Serum IgE
nodes.description: Immunoglobulin associated with allergic/type-2 immune responses.
nodes.clinical_relevance: IgE class switching driven by IL-4; elevated in allergy, parasitic infection, IgE myeloma (rare); omalizumab dosing based on baseline total IgE level; clinical note: total IgE rises during omalizumab treatment (drug-bound IgE detectable) → measure free IgE not total IgE to monitor omalizumab response; tryptase + IgE elevated → confirms mast cell-mediated anaphylaxis vs other causes

nodes.name: Interferon-stimulated gene signature
nodes.description: Gene-expression pattern reflecting interferon pathway activity.
nodes.clinical_relevance: 75% of SLE patients IFN-signature-high; predicts anifrolumab response (TULIP-1/2: IFN-high patients show greater BICLA response); AI single-cell discovery: ISG15+ macrophage subpopulation is exclusive to Class III/IV lupus nephritis (explains why anifrolumab works in proliferative but not membranous LN); interferon score also elevated in Sjögren's, dermatomyositis, systemic sclerosis

nodes.name: ATTRACT
nodes.description: Pivotal rheumatoid arthritis trial evaluating infliximab with methotrexate.
source_refs: Lipsky PE et al. N Engl J Med 2000
aliases: Anti-TNF Trial in RA with Concomitant Therapy
nodes.clinical_relevance: N=428; infliximab vs placebo in MTX-inadequate RA (1999-2000); first biologic to demonstrate structural protection (Sharp score, joint erosion slowed, not just symptom improvement); established anti-TNF as standard RA care and the template for biologic trial design

nodes.name: CANTOS
nodes.description: Trial testing IL-1β inhibition with canakinumab in inflammatory cardiovascular disease.
source_refs: Ridker PM et al. N Engl J Med 2017
nodes.clinical_relevance: N=10,061; canakinumab (anti-IL-1β) vs placebo in post-MI patients with hsCRP >2mg/L; MACE -15% (HR 0.85, p=0.021); LDL unchanged → first clinical proof macrophage NLRP3-IL-1β causally drives CVD (not just lipid storage); lung cancer mortality -77% (unexpected, IL-1β promotes TME); colchicine (COLCOT: -23%; LoDoCo-2: -31%) validated same mechanism cheaply

nodes.name: KEYNOTE-006
nodes.description: Randomized trial of pembrolizumab versus ipilimumab in advanced melanoma.
source_refs: Robert C et al. N Engl J Med 2015; Lancet Oncol 2019 (5-yr)
nodes.clinical_relevance: N=834; pembrolizumab vs ipilimumab in advanced melanoma; 5yr OS: 38.7% vs 31.1% (p<0.001); irAE grade 3-4: 17% vs 27%; showed the PD-1 axis outperformed the CTLA-4 axis in melanoma; established anti-PD-1 as first-line for all PD-L1+ advanced cancers

nodes.name: ERASURE
nodes.description: Phase 3 psoriasis trial of secukinumab.
source_refs: Langley RG et al. N Engl J Med 2014
aliases: Efficacy of Response and Safety of Two Fixed Secukinumab Regimens
nodes.clinical_relevance: N=738; secukinumab vs placebo in moderate-severe plaque psoriasis; PASI 90 at week 12: 150mg 59.2%, 300mg 77.1% vs placebo 4.9%; established IL-17A blockade efficacy in psoriasis; foundational for anti-IL-17A approval

nodes.name: LIBERTY AD
nodes.description: Dupilumab clinical-trial programme in atopic dermatitis.
source_refs: Simpson EL et al. N Engl J Med 2016
nodes.clinical_relevance: SOLO 1 (N=671) + SOLO 2 (N=708); dupilumab 300mg Q2W vs placebo in moderate-severe AD; IGA 0/1 clear/almost clear: 38% vs 10% (SOLO-1); EASI-75: 51% vs 15%; established dupilumab as transformative AD therapy; launched the type-2 inflammation biologic era

nodes.name: PD-1
nodes.description: Programmed Death-1: inhibitory receptor on activated/exhausted T cells (and NK cells). PD-L1/PD-L2 binding → SHP-2 → ZAP-70 dephosphorylation → T cell inactivation. Central cancer immune escape checkpoint.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Anti-PD-1 (pembrolizumab, nivolumab) is the most widely used checkpoint blockade. Progenitor exhausted T cells (TCF-1+/PD-1+/TIM-3-) respond; terminal exhausted (TOX+/TCF-1-) do NOT. Morning infusion timing → superior OS (HR 0.83, Lancet Oncology 2023)

nodes.name: PD-L1
nodes.description: Programmed Death Ligand 1: upregulated on tumour cells (oncogenic EGFR/KRAS/PI3K/MYC → STAT3 → PD-L1) and by adaptive immune resistance (TIL IFN-γ → JAK1/2 → STAT1 → PD-L1). Also on APCs (normal immune homeostasis).
nodes.clinical_relevance: PD-L1 TPS/CPS used as predictive biomarker: TPS ≥50% → pembrolizumab monotherapy NSCLC (KEYnote-024); CPS ≥10 → TNBC, gastric, HNSCC. Anti-PD-L1: atezolizumab, durvalumab, avelumab

nodes.name: CTLA-4
nodes.description: Cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen 4: constitutively expressed on Tregs; upregulated on activated effector T cells. Competes with CD28 for B7 (CD80/CD86) binding with higher affinity → removes Signal 2. Trans-endocytosis of B7 from APCs (Treg CTLA-4 mechanism). Tumour Treg CTLA-4 → ipilimumab ADCC depletes intratumoural Tregs.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Ipilimumab (IgG1 Fc-active → macrophage ADCC depletes tumour Tregs, primary anti-tumour mechanism, not co-stimulation blockade); tremelimumab (IgG2, poor ADCC, inferior as monotherapy). Abatacept (CTLA-4-Ig) blocks B7 → T cell anergy in RA (opposite therapeutic use)

nodes.name: FcεRI
nodes.description: High-affinity IgE receptor (Kd ~10^-10 M) constitutively expressed on mast cells and basophils. Allergen-specific IgE loads FcεRI → allergen crosslinks ≥2 adjacent FcεRI → Lyn/Syk → PLCγ → Ca2+ release → degranulation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Omalizumab (anti-IgE → free IgE falls → FcεRI receptor downregulates because receptor requires ligand for surface expression) → reduces mast cell/basophil arming; OUtMATCH: 67% of peanut-allergic children tolerated 600mg peanut protein (FDA 2024)

nodes.name: BCR
nodes.description: B cell receptor: membrane-bound immunoglobulin (IgM initially, class-switched after GC) + Igα/Igβ signalling subunits. Recognises native 3D protein antigen (no MHC restriction, contrast with TCR). V(D)J recombination → 10^12 diversity; SHM in GC → affinity maturation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: BCR signalling → BTK → NF-κB; BTK inhibitors (ibrutinib, zanubrutinib, acalabrutinib) approved for B-NHL/CLL/WM; BCR diversity enables antibody response to any antigen shape

nodes.name: TCR
nodes.description: T cell receptor: αβ heterodimer (or γδ) + CD3 complex (ε,γ,δ,ζ). Recognises processed peptide-MHC (Signal 1). V(D)J recombination → 10^15-18 TCR diversity. CD4 co-receptor (MHC-II) or CD8 co-receptor (MHC-I) stabilises TCR-pMHC interaction.
nodes.clinical_relevance: CAR (chimeric antigen receptor) replaces TCR variable regions with antibody-derived scFv → MHC-independent recognition (bypasses MHC-I downregulation cancer escape); tebentafusp = TCR-based bispecific (gp100/HLA-A*02:01 × CD3)

nodes.name: IL-4Rα
nodes.description: IL-4 receptor alpha chain: shared subunit between Type I (IL-4Rα/γc → IL-4 only, haematopoietic cells) and Type II (IL-4Rα/IL-13Rα1 → IL-4 and IL-13, non-haematopoietic cells including epithelium and smooth muscle). Signals via JAK1/JAK3 → STAT6 → GATA-3.
nodes.clinical_relevance: DUPILUMAB (anti-IL-4Rα) blocks both IL-4 and IL-13 simultaneously via Type II receptor → broadest biologic indication (AD, asthma, CRSwNP, EoE, prurigo nodularis, COPD T2); conjunctivitis SE (10-28%) = IL-4/13 regulate ocular goblet cells → mechanistic prediction

nodes.name: IFNAR1
nodes.description: Interferon alpha/beta receptor subunit 1: with IFNAR2 forms the type I IFN receptor complex → JAK1/TYK2 → STAT1/STAT2 + IRF9 → ISGF3 complex → ISGs (IFIT1, MX1, OAS1, ISG15).
nodes.clinical_relevance: Anifrolumab (anti-IFNAR1): blocks ALL type I IFNs (α, β, ω) simultaneously → FDA 2021 for moderate-severe SLE (TULIP-2: BICLA 47.8% vs 31.5%); IFN-signature-high patients respond better; ISG15+ macrophage exclusive to Class III/IV LN (AI discovery explains mechanistic selectivity)

nodes.name: BAFF
nodes.description: B cell activating factor: produced by monocytes, DCs, neutrophils; IFN-α directly upregulates BAFF transcription in monocytes (connecting pDC IFN-α → B cell rescue in SLE). BAFFR/TACI/BCMA → NF-κB → B cell survival. Rescues autoreactive B cells that should be deleted by peripheral tolerance.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Belimumab (anti-BAFF/BLyS): first biologic approved for SLE in 50 years (BLISS-52/76 2011, 48% annual flare rate reduction); best in: IFN-high + elevated anti-dsDNA + active non-renal manifestations; does NOT reach plasma cells (CD20-negative); atacicept (TACI-Ig) traps BAFF+APRIL → depletes B cells AND plasma cells

nodes.name: APRIL
nodes.description: A proliferation-inducing ligand: binds TACI and BCMA on plasma cells → plasma cell survival in bone marrow niche; shares TACI with BAFF. Atacicept (TACI-Ig) blocks both BAFF and APRIL → depletes B cells AND long-lived plasma cells (unlike belimumab which blocks BAFF only and thus spares plasma cells).
nodes.clinical_relevance: Key distinction from BAFF: APRIL maintains long-lived plasma cell survival in bone marrow → explains why belimumab (anti-BAFF only) spares plasma cells; atacicept (BAFF+APRIL trap) Phase 3 NEPTUNE (SLE) data expected 2025-2026

nodes.name: Type I interferon
nodes.description: IFN-α (produced mainly by pDCs, 13 subtypes) and IFN-β (produced by most nucleated cells on viral dsRNA sensing via RIG-I/MDA5/cGAS-STING). IFNAR1/2 → JAK1/TYK2 → STAT1/STAT2 → ISGs (IFIT1, MX1, OAS1, antiviral state); MHC-I upregulation; DC maturation; B cell activation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: SLE: NET-released DNA → pDC TLR7/9 → IFN-α → BAFF → autoreactive B cell rescue. IFN-β (therapeutic) for MS: reduces RRMS relapse rate via DC and T cell modulation. 75% of SLE patients IFN-signature-high → predictive biomarker for anifrolumab

nodes.name: PD-L2
nodes.description: Programmed Death Ligand 2: second PD-1 ligand (lower expression than PD-L1); predominantly on APCs (DCs, macrophages); IL-4 induces PD-L2 expression (Th2 context, different from PD-L1 which is IFN-γ-inducible in Th1/TME). Some anti-PD-1 drugs may work partly via PD-L2 pathway.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Less clinically targeted than PD-L1; anti-PD-1 blocks both PD-L1 and PD-L2 interactions (vs anti-PD-L1 drugs which only block PD-L1/PD-1); anti-PD-L2 ICI not yet clinically developed

nodes.name: IL-2
nodes.description: T cell autocrine growth factor: produced by activated CD4+ T cells; IL-2Rα (CD25, high-affinity chain, highest on Tregs) + IL-2Rβ (CD122) + IL-2Rγ (γc); JAK1/JAK3 → STAT5. Autocrine survival signal driving clonal expansion. Low-dose IL-2 selectively expands Tregs (highest CD25 expression = highest sensitivity to low IL-2).
nodes.clinical_relevance: LOW-dose IL-2 (1-3M IU SC, 5-day cycles): preferentially expands Tregs (CD25 high) → Phase 2 SLE (SLEDAI 8.1→4.7, Tregs 4-fold expansion); Phase 2 cGVHD, T1DM. High-dose IL-2 (cancer): toxic due to capillary leak syndrome at doses required for effector T cell expansion

nodes.name: IL-33
nodes.description: IL-1 family alarmin; released by stressed/necrotic epithelial cells; binds ST2 receptor on ILC2, mast cells, Th2 cells, Tregs → NF-κB + MAPK → type-2 cytokine cascade. Potent ILC2 activator alongside TSLP and IL-25. Drives type-2 inflammation in allergy, asthma, AD.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Itepekimab (anti-IL-33, REGN3500): Phase 3 asthma (LIBERTY ASTHMA QUEST). Tezostumab (anti-ST2). Works upstream similarly to tezepelumab (anti-TSLP); combined TSLP+IL-33 blockade rationale in severe type-2 disease

nodes.name: TSLP
nodes.description: Thymic stromal lymphopoietin: epithelial cell-derived alarmin released by stressed epithelium (FLG mutation, ozone, cigarette smoke, allergens); activates ILC2 and DCs → Th2 polarisation via OX40L upregulation; acts upstream of IL-4/IL-5/IL-13 axis; also activates mast cells and basophils.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Tezepelumab (anti-TSLP, Tezspire): NAVIGATOR trial (N=1061), 56% exacerbation reduction across ALL asthma endotypes (including low-eosinophil, triple-negative for biologics); first asthma biologic effective across all endotypes because it blocks the broadest upstream signal

nodes.name: Complement C3
nodes.description: Central complement protein: all three activation pathways (classical via immune complexes, lectin via mannose, alternative via microbial surfaces) converge on C3 convertase → C3b (opsonin) + C3a (anaphylatoxin, mast cell activator). Critical for IC clearance (deficiency → SLE susceptibility, homozygous C1q deficiency = strongest single-gene SLE risk).
nodes.clinical_relevance: C3 consumption (low C3) = SLE disease activity marker (especially LN); together with C4 and anti-dsDNA, tracks LN flares. Complement deficiency: C1q deficiency → SLE (immune complex clearance failure); C3 deficiency → recurrent encapsulated bacteria; terminal complement deficiency (C5-C9) → Neisseria specifically

nodes.name: IgG
nodes.description: Class-switched, high-affinity immunoglobulin: produced by plasma cells (bone marrow-resident long-lived, and short-lived GC-derived). 4 subclasses (IgG1-4) with different effector functions. IgG1 (most common): high ADCC (FcγRIIIa), CDC (C1q binding), placental transfer (FcRn). IgG4: no CDC, poor ADCC, Fab arm exchange → bispecific-like.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Secondary antibody deficiency: anti-CD20 (rituximab/ocrelizumab) repeated courses → IgG <5g/L → recurrent infections → SCIG replacement needed. IgG4-RD: IgG4-secreting plasmablasts (target of inebilizumab anti-CD19). Certolizumab (anti-TNF): Fab' fragment, no IgG Fc → no placental transfer via FcRn → preferred in pregnancy

nodes.name: Adenosine
nodes.description: Produced from ATP by CD39 (NTPDase1, extracellular) → AMP → CD73 (ecto-5'-nucleotidase) → adenosine; binds A2AR on T cells, NK cells, DCs → cAMP → suppression of effector function. Major TME immunosuppressive signal. Treg CD39/CD73 activity generates adenosine → effector T cell suppression.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Adenosine in TME: pathway includes Tregs (CD39+CD73) + tumour CD73; A2AR antagonists (AZD4635, ciforadenant) in Phase 1/2 ICI combinations; CD73 blockade (oleclumab, anti-CD73 Phase 2)

nodes.name: Type 1 diabetes
nodes.description: Immune-mediated destruction of pancreatic beta cells: CD8+ CTL (nPOD histology dominant) + CD4+ Th1 + macrophage insulitis → beta cell death → absolute insulin deficiency. Autoantibodies (GAD65, IA-2, ZnT8, preproinsulin insulin autoantibodies) detectable years before clinical onset.
nodes.clinical_relevance: TN10 TEPLIZUMAB TRIAL (2019/FDA 2022): anti-CD3 Fc-silent → Th1:Treg ratio shift in islets → T1DM onset delayed 25 months (HR 0.41, p=0.006), the first drug shown to delay an autoimmune disease. Stage 2 T1DM (autoantibodies + dysglycaemia, no clinical T1DM) = the therapeutic window

nodes.name: ANCA vasculitis
nodes.description: ANCA (anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody) IgG produced by B cells: anti-PR3 (cytoplasmic ANCA, GPA) or anti-MPO (perinuclear ANCA, MPA). ANCA binds cytoplasmic antigens (PR3, MPO) expressed on surface of cytokine-primed neutrophils → FcγRIII activation → neutrophil activation inside vessel wall → necrotising vasculitis.
nodes.clinical_relevance: RAVE TRIAL (2010/FDA 2011): rituximab vs cyclophosphamide induction → CR 64% vs 53%; ANCA titres undetectable in 90% of rituximab responders → proved B cell→ANCA→neutrophil chain is causal; rituximab superior for relapsing disease. ANCA titre monitoring standard of care

nodes.name: Lupus nephritis
nodes.description: Class III/IV LN (proliferative): immune complex (anti-dsDNA IgG + complement) deposition in glomeruli → podocyte injury → proteinuria → CKD. ISG15+ macrophage subpopulation exclusive to Class III/IV (AI scRNA-seq discovery). APOL1 G1/G2 variants (African ancestry, 20-25%) → independent podocyte vulnerability → worse outcomes.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Treatment evolution: MMF+voclosporin (CNI, AURORA: 41% CRR vs 23% MMF alone); obinutuzumab+MMF (NOBILITY: 50% vs 30% CRR at 2yr, FDA 2025). APOL1 not routinely tested → equity gap. Faricimab (anti-VEGF/Ang2) in LN Phase 2

nodes.name: Graft-versus-host disease
nodes.description: Donor T cells recognise host alloantigens → alloresponse. aGVHD: T cell-driven (ruxolitinib, steroids, cyclosporine); cGVHD: macrophage-fibrosis-driven (CSF-1R+ macrophages → TGF-β → fibroblast activation → collagen deposition in skin/lung/liver). PTCy (days +3/+4 post-HSCT) selectively kills alloreactive donor T cells (cycling → more drug exposure).
nodes.clinical_relevance: Ruxolitinib (JAK1/2): REACH-2/3 trials → FDA approved aGVHD and cGVHD; axatilimab (anti-CSF-1R mAb): AGAVE-201 → ORR 74% in 3rd+ line cGVHD (FDA 2024, first drug specifically targeting cGVHD fibrosis biology); PTCy enables haploidentical HSCT (~95% of patients have a haploidentical donor)

nodes.name: Cancer immune escape
nodes.description: Progressive immunoediting of tumour cells under immune selection pressure: Elimination (most transformed cells killed by NK/CTL) → Equilibrium (tumour cells survive under continuous immune pressure, selected for immune resistance) → Escape (clinical cancer: MHC-I loss, PD-L1 upregulation, Treg accumulation, cold tumour, antigen loss). Every clinical cancer has survived decades of immune pressure.
nodes.clinical_relevance: WNT/β-catenin activation (25-35% melanoma) → cold tumour → anti-PD-1 non-response; SLC6A4 on NK cells suppresses anti-tumour cytotoxicity (AI multi-omics → fluoxetine+pembrolizumab Phase 2 NSCLC 2024)

nodes.name: Rituximab
nodes.description: Chimeric IgG1 (human Fc + murine variable region) anti-CD20 mAb: ADCC (FcγRIIIa on NK cells), CDC (C1q → MAC), and direct apoptosis signalling. Depletes CD20+ B cells (naive, GC, memory) but NOT plasma cells (CD20-negative). RA, ANCA vasculitis, DLBCL, FL, CLL, MS (off-label/ocrelizumab preferred), ITP, pemphigus.
nodes.clinical_relevance: RAVE trial (ANCA vasculitis): rituximab = standard induction; BSRBR: serious infection monitoring; secondary antibody deficiency: IgG monitoring 6-monthly with repeat dosing; biosimilars available (rituximab-abbs, -pvvr); IV infusion (slow first dose, infusion reactions); NOT equivalent to ocrelizumab for MS (ocrelizumab humanised → less immunogenic, PPMS approved)

nodes.name: Ocrelizumab
nodes.description: Humanised IgG1 anti-CD20 mAb: lower immunogenicity than rituximab (human Fc+variable), similar ADCC mechanism. RRMS and PPMS (Ocrelizumab is the only FDA-approved PPMS therapy). SC formulation available 2023. Mechanism in MS: depletes leptomeningeal B cell aggregates that drive compartmentalised CNS inflammation in progressive MS.
nodes.clinical_relevance: ORATORIO trial (PPMS): first ever positive Phase 3 trial in PPMS history (CDP slowed 24%, HR 0.76, p=0.003), supported a B-cell contribution to progressive MS. 15 years of failed T cell-targeting trials preceded this. IgG monitoring 6-monthly. Hypersensitivity: premedication (methylprednisolone, antihistamine, paracetamol)

nodes.name: Teplizumab
nodes.description: Anti-CD3 Fc-silent mAb (Fc modified to prevent ADCC/CDC): binds CD3ε on T cells without Fc receptor engagement → T cell exhaustion/regulatory programme in autoreactive Th1 cells driving insulitis → shifts Th1:Treg ratio in islets. Does not globally deplete T cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: TN10 TRIAL (2019/FDA 2022): first drug to delay an autoimmune disease. Stage 2 T1DM (autoantibodies + dysglycaemia) → 14-day IV course → T1DM onset delayed 25 months (HR 0.41, p=0.006). Template for Stage 2 autoimmune intervention across all autoimmune diseases. Transient EBV-like syndrome during infusion (managed with paracetamol)

nodes.name: Baricitinib
nodes.description: Selective JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor (oral, once daily): blocks multiple cytokine pathways (IL-6, IFN-α/β, GM-CSF) + AAK1 inhibition (reduces viral endocytosis). Approved: RA, AD, alopecia areata, COVID-19 ARDS. A knowledge-graph screen proposed JAK1/2 plus AAK1 inhibition for COVID-19 in early 2020, before the trial programme tested it.
nodes.clinical_relevance: FDA 2021 boxed warning for JAK inhibitors in patients ≥50y with ≥1 CV risk factor (MACE/VTE/malignancy/infection; ORAL SURVEILLANCE trial). ACTT-2 trial (COVID-19): hospitalization duration reduced vs remdesivir. COV-BARRIER: survival benefit in severe COVID-19. FDA approved for COVID-19 2022, total discovery-to-approval: 15 months (vs conventional 15 years)

nodes.name: Anifrolumab
nodes.description: Human IgG1κ anti-IFNAR1 mAb: blocks ALL type I interferons (IFN-α, IFN-β, IFN-ω) simultaneously by targeting receptor subunit 1. Downstream of pDC IFN-α production. FDA approved 2021 for moderate-severe SLE (first new SLE mechanism biologic since belimumab 2011). IFN-signature-high patients respond better (75% of SLE patients).
nodes.clinical_relevance: TULIP-2 (N=362): BICLA 47.8% vs 31.5% placebo; TULIP-1 (missed primary endpoint due to endpoint selection issue, different composite); ISG15+ macrophage exclusive to Class III/IV LN (AI discovery explains why anifrolumab may have differential LN class efficacy). IFN gene signature score used as companion diagnostic/enrichment strategy

nodes.name: Cilta-cel
nodes.description: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel: BCMA-targeting CAR-T with 4-1BB co-stimulatory domain + DUAL BCMA-binding scFv (higher avidity → kills cells with lower BCMA expression; reduces antigen escape). 4-1BB → sustained oxidative phosphorylation-biased T cell memory → superior long-term persistence vs CD28 co-stim.
nodes.clinical_relevance: CARTITUDE-4 (N=419): cilta-cel vs SoC in 1-3 prior line MM → PFS HR 0.26 (74% reduction in progression/death risk); 12-month PFS 76% vs 49%; ORR 84% vs 67%; one of the largest PFS benefits in any randomised oncology trial. CAR-T moving from 4th-line last resort to 2nd-line standard. CRS grade 3+: 5-8%; ICANS: 15-20%

nodes.name: Blinatumomab
nodes.description: Anti-CD3 × anti-CD19 BiTE (bispecific T cell engager, 55kDa tandem scFv): one arm grabs CD3 on any T cell, other arm grabs CD19 on B cell/tumour → forced T cell-tumour cell contact → CTL-mediated killing WITHOUT requiring MHC-I, antigen presentation, or prior T cell sensitisation. First BiTE approved (FDA 2014, B-ALL).
nodes.clinical_relevance: B-ALL CR rate ~40% in heavily pre-treated; DLBCL (3rd-line+): ORR 43%; Step-up dosing protocol (9μg → 28μg over first 2 weeks) to prevent severe CRS. short half-life (2h) → continuous IV infusion 4-week cycles. lower CRS rate than CAR-T (2-8% grade 3+), no massive in vivo expansion; off-the-shelf (vs CAR-T: 3-4 week manufacture)

nodes.name: Belimumab
nodes.description: Human IgG1λ anti-BAFF/BLyS mAb: neutralises soluble BAFF → reduces B cell survival signal → autoreactive B cells more likely to undergo apoptosis. Does NOT block APRIL (which binds TACI and BCMA on plasma cells) → does NOT deplete plasma cells. IV + SC formulation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: First biologic approved for SLE in 50 years (BLISS-52/76 2011): annualised flare rate -48% vs placebo; best in: IFN-high + elevated anti-dsDNA + active non-renal SLE + elevated BAFF at baseline; HCQ must continue; SC formulation (200mg weekly) enables home administration. ATACICEPT (TACI-Ig) blocks BAFF+APRIL → depletes plasma cells too (Phase 3 NEPTUNE data 2025)

nodes.name: Inebilizumab
nodes.description: Humanised IgG1κ anti-CD19 mAb with afucosylation (enhanced NK ADCC): targets ALL CD19+ cells including naive B cells, GC B cells, memory B cells, AND PLASMABLASTS (CD20-negative, CD19+). Reaches the plasmablast compartment that rituximab misses.
nodes.clinical_relevance: MITIGATE trial (IgG4-related disease, N=135): inebilizumab 87% flare reduction vs 39% placebo (primary endpoint met) → FDA approved IgG4-RD 2025. NMOSD (anti-AQP4 IgG): N-MOmentum trial → FDA approved 2020. Plasmablasts are the dominant pathogenic cell in IgG4-RD → reaching CD19+ plasmablasts is the mechanistic basis of superiority over rituximab

nodes.name: Deucravacitinib
nodes.description: First allosteric kinase inhibitor approved in immunology: binds JH2 pseudokinase regulatory domain of TYK2 (NOT the ATP-binding active JH1 domain). JH2 of TYK2 structurally distinct from JAK1/2/3 JH2 domains → highly selective inhibition of TYK2-dependent receptors (IL-12R, IL-23R, IFN-αβR) without meaningful JAK1/2/3 activity.
nodes.clinical_relevance: FDA approved 2022 for moderate-severe plaque psoriasis. POETYK-PSO-1/2: PASI 75 53% vs 9% placebo vs 35% apremilast; PASI 90: 37% vs 2% vs 22%. NO JAK class boxed warning (FDA 2021), TYK2 selectivity avoids JAK1/2/3-dependent haematopoiesis/cardiac effects. First allosteric kinase inhibitor: paradigm for future selectivity engineering

nodes.name: Omalizumab
nodes.description: Humanised IgG1κ anti-IgE mAb: binds free IgE (same epitope as FcεRI binding site on IgE) → prevents IgE loading onto mast cells/basophils → FcεRI receptor downregulates (requires IgE ligand for surface expression) → less mast cell arming → reduced degranulation response to allergens. Not allergen-specific → prevents all IgE-mediated reactions simultaneously.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Approved: severe allergic asthma, CSU (urticaria ASTERIA I+II: CR 36% vs 8%), food allergy (OUtMATCH 2024: 67% tolerated peanut challenge - FDA 2024). Monthly SC. Total IgE rises (drug-bound IgE detected) → monitor free IgE not total IgE. Tryptase-confirmed anaphylaxis + elevated total IgE = eligible

nodes.name: Tezepelumab
nodes.description: Human IgG2λ anti-TSLP mAb: blocks TSLP (thymic stromal lymphopoietin) the upstream epithelial alarmin. TSLP activates ILC2 AND DCs (→Th2) AND mast cells AND basophils → blocking TSLP prevents ALL downstream type-2 inflammation simultaneously, regardless of the dominant effector cell.
nodes.clinical_relevance: NAVIGATOR trial (N=1061): 56% exacerbation reduction vs placebo in severe asthma across all endotypes (including low-eosinophil, triple-negative for other biologics). First asthma biologic effective in ALL endotypes. Monthly SC injection. Works upstream of IL-4/IL-5/IL-13/IL-33 axis

nodes.name: RAVE
nodes.description: Rituximab versus Cyclophosphamide for ANCA-Associated Vasculitis. N=197, Phase 3, 2010. Rituximab vs cyclophosphamide induction in ANCA GPA/MPA.
nodes.clinical_relevance: CR 64% rituximab vs 53% cyclophosphamide (non-inferior). ANCA titres undetectable in 90% of rituximab responders. superior for relapsing disease. proved B cell→ANCA→neutrophil FcγRIII activation chain is causal. First trial to establish rituximab as ANCA vasculitis induction standard
source_refs: Stone JH et al. N Engl J Med 2010

nodes.name: ORATORIO
nodes.description: Ocrelizumab vs placebo in primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS). N=732, Phase 3, 2016. First positive Phase 3 PPMS trial in history.
nodes.clinical_relevance: 24% slower CDP (HR 0.76, p=0.003). First ever positive Phase 3 PPMS trial after 15 years of failed T cell-targeting trials. Proved B cells (not T cells) drive progressive MS. Ocrelizumab became first and only approved PPMS therapy. Drove BTK inhibitor development for PPMS (tolebrutinib HERCULES Phase 3 2024)
source_refs: Montalban X et al. N Engl J Med 2017

nodes.name: TN10 Teplizumab
nodes.description: TrialNet 10: anti-CD3 Fc-silent (teplizumab) vs placebo in relatives with Stage 2 T1DM (≥2 autoantibodies + dysglycaemia). N=76. 2019 published; FDA approved as Tzield 2022.
nodes.clinical_relevance: T1DM onset delayed median 25 months (HR 0.41, p=0.006). the first drug shown to delay an autoimmune disease. Implicated CD4+ Th1 imbalance in islets is causal and modifiable. Established Stage 2 autoimmune intervention as a viable therapeutic window. Template for all autoimmune prevention trials
source_refs: Herold KC et al. N Engl J Med 2019

nodes.name: RECOVERY
nodes.description: RECOVERY (Randomised Evaluation of COVID-19 Therapy): UK-wide adaptive platform trial >40,000 patients across multiple arms. Identified dexamethasone, tocilizumab, baricitinib, and others. Gold standard for adaptive trial design.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Dexamethasone: 28-day mortality 23% vs 26% oxygen-requiring (RR 0.64); RR 1.19 harm in non-oxygen-requiring (viral phase). Estimated 1 million lives saved. Fastest translation from trial to worldwide practice in medical history (6 weeks). Proved macrophage IL-6 drives COVID-19 ARDS mortality
source_refs: RECOVERY Collaborative Group. N Engl J Med 2021

nodes.name: CARTITUDE-4
nodes.description: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) vs standard of care (PVd or DPd) in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma after 1-3 prior lines. N=419.
nodes.clinical_relevance: PFS HR 0.26 (74% reduction in progression/death risk); 12-month PFS 76% vs 49%; ORR 84% vs 67%. One of the largest PFS benefits in any randomised oncology trial. Moved CAR-T from 4th-line to 2nd-line standard. Proved 4-1BB co-stim + dual scFv design = durable responses
source_refs: San-Miguel J et al. N Engl J Med 2023

nodes.name: Anti-dsDNA antibody
nodes.description: IgG antibodies against double-stranded DNA: produced by autoreactive GC B cells (Tfh-dependent) in SLE; form immune complexes → complement activation → glomerular deposition → lupus nephritis. Titre correlates with disease activity (especially LN).
nodes.clinical_relevance: Standard SLE monitoring biomarker: rising anti-dsDNA + falling C3/C4 = LN flare predictor. Belimumab reduces anti-dsDNA titres (PD biomarker confirming BAFF blockade → less autoreactive B cell rescue → less GC → less anti-dsDNA production)

nodes.name: ACPA
nodes.description: Anti-citrullinated protein antibodies: IgG directed against citrullinated proteins (fibrinogen, vimentin, α-enolase, collagen) generated by PAD2/4 enzymes in inflamed synovium. Detectable 5-10 years before clinical RA. High specificity for RA (>95%). Titre >3× ULN = seropositive RA.
nodes.clinical_relevance: High-titre ACPA has been linked to better abatacept response in observational cohorts; guidelines do not mandate a specific biologic; ACPA titre falls with rituximab (PD biomarker in RAVE-like trials confirming B cell → ACPA chain)

nodes.name: ANCA
nodes.description: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies: PR3-ANCA (cytoplasmic pattern, c-ANCA) in GPA or MPO-ANCA (perinuclear pattern, p-ANCA) in MPA; IgG produced by B cells; binds cytoplasmic antigens expressed on surface of cytokine-primed neutrophils → FcγRIII activation → vessel wall destruction.
nodes.clinical_relevance: RAVE trial: ANCA titres fell to undetectable in 90% of rituximab responders → pharmacodynamic proof that B cells produce ANCA. Rising ANCA titre predicts relapse → guides prophylactic rituximab re-dosing decisions. Distinguishes GPA (PR3-ANCA) from MPA (MPO-ANCA) with prognostic implications

nodes.name: Tryptase
nodes.description: Mast cell granule protease: released during mast cell degranulation; serum tryptase peak at 60-90 minutes post-anaphylaxis; baseline tryptase elevated in systemic mastocytosis (SM) and hereditary alpha-tryptasemia. Diagnostic for anaphylaxis and SM.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Anaphylaxis diagnosis: acute tryptase ≥(1.2×baseline + 2μg/L) confirms mast cell activation. Systemic mastocytosis: baseline tryptase >20ng/mL. KIT D816V mutation → avapritinib (SM). Monthly tryptase monitoring tracks SM response to avapritinib

nodes.name: TMB
nodes.description: Tumour mutational burden: total number of somatic mutations per megabase of coding sequence, quantified by tissue NGS (FoundationOne CDx, FDA-approved biomarker). High TMB (≥10 mut/Mb) → more neoantigens → more TILs → more PD-1+ exhausted CTLs available for rescue by anti-PD-1.
nodes.clinical_relevance: FDA approved pembrolizumab for TMB-H ≥10 mut/Mb solid tumours (tumour-agnostic, 2020; KEYnote-158). AI quantification from tissue NGS (FoundationOne CDx, Tempus xT). MSI-H and TMB-H overlap but are not identical. Both approved independently. High TMB in hypermutator cancers (MMR-deficient, POLE-mutant)

nodes.name: PD-L1 expression
nodes.description: Tumour PD-L1 expression by immunohistochemistry (IHC): TPS (tumour proportion score: % tumour cells staining ≥1+) for NSCLC/HNSCC; CPS (combined positive score: PD-L1+ tumour + immune + stromal cells per 100 tumour cells) for TNBC/gastric/cervical/endometrial. Dynamic: upregulated by IFN-γ from TILs (adaptive immune resistance).
nodes.clinical_relevance: NSCLC: TPS ≥50% → pembrolizumab monotherapy first-line (KEYnote-024: OS HR 0.62). TPS 1-49% + chemo backbone. limitation: PD-L1 is dynamic, heterogeneous, assessed on pre-treatment biopsy (may not represent whole tumour at treatment); negative PD-L1 does not exclude response (MSI-H/TMB-H patients can respond with PD-L1 negative)

nodes.name: cGAS-STING pathway
nodes.description: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase → STING: cGAS binds cytoplasmic dsDNA (always abnormal: viral, tumour genomic instability, mitochondrial damage, NET DNA in SLE) → produces cGAMP (cyclic dinucleotide) → activates STING (ER-resident adaptor) → TBK1 → IRF3 → IFN-β + NF-κB.
nodes.clinical_relevance: 2023 Lasker Award. clinical applications: STING agonists (diABZI, ADU-S100): intratumoral DC activation → cross-presentation of tumour neoantigens → CTL priming (heating cold tumours); STING inhibitors: SLE interferonopathy pipeline (chronic cGAS-STING activation from NETs). Tumours with absent STING activity = cold tumour phenotype

nodes.name: V(D)J recombination
nodes.description: RAG1/RAG2 endonuclease-mediated combinatorial joining of Variable, Diversity, and Joining immunoglobulin/TCR gene segments + N-nucleotide addition at junctions → 10^15-18 receptor diversity. Heavy chain: V+D+J. Light chain/TCR α: V+J. TCR β: V+D+J.
nodes.clinical_relevance: RAG1/RAG2 mutations → RAG-SCID (no T or B cells, no V(D)J recombination); CAR-T bypasses this system (synthetic antigen receptor). Repertoire diversity = basis of adaptive immunity; narrow repertoire in elderly (thymic involution → homeostatic proliferation → oligoclonal TCR repertoire → reduced vaccine responses

nodes.name: Complement cascade
nodes.description: Three pathways (classical/lectin/alternative) converging on C3 convertase → C3b (opsonin) + C3a (anaphylatoxin) + C5 convertase → C5a (potent chemotactic factor) + C5b → MAC (C5b-9 membrane attack complex, pore formation → Neisseria killing).
nodes.clinical_relevance: C1q deficiency → SLE (most severe SLE genetics: immune complex clearance failure); C3 deficiency → encapsulated bacteria; Terminal complement deficiency (C5-C9) → Neisseria specifically (only organism killed exclusively by MAC). Eculizumab (anti-C5 → blocks MAC): PNH, aHUS, NMO, mandates meningococcal vaccination (eculizumab recreates terminal complement deficiency)

nodes.name: Basophil
nodes.description: Rare granulocyte; FcεRI-armed source of histamine, IL-4 and IL-13 that can initiate type-2 responses.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Basophilia in CML; basophil activation test in drug/food allergy; contributes to chronic urticaria.

nodes.name: γδ T cell
nodes.description: T cells with γδ TCR sensing phosphoantigens via butyrophilins (BTN3A1/BTN2A1) and stress ligands (NKG2D); rapid IL-17/IFN-γ in barrier tissues.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Dermal γδ T cells are an early IL-17 source in psoriasis models; Vγ9Vδ2 cells explored for tumour immunotherapy.

nodes.name: MAIT cell
nodes.description: Mucosal-associated invariant T cells recognise microbial riboflavin metabolites (5-OP-RU) on MR1; abundant in liver and mucosa.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Circulating MAIT cells are depleted in severe COVID-19 and sepsis.

nodes.name: iNKT cell
nodes.description: Invariant NKT cells recognise lipid antigens (e.g., α-GalCer) on CD1d and rapidly release IL-4 and IFN-γ.

nodes.name: Myeloid-derived suppressor cell
nodes.description: Immature myeloid cells expanded in cancer and chronic inflammation that suppress T cells via arginase-1, iNOS, ROS and IL-10.
nodes.clinical_relevance: High circulating MDSC levels associate with poorer checkpoint-inhibitor outcomes in several cancers.

nodes.name: Memory T cell
nodes.description: Antigen-experienced T cells (central, effector and tissue-resident memory) that respond faster and stronger on re-exposure.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Basis of durable vaccine protection; tissue-resident memory T cells drive relapsing psoriasis and vitiligo patches.

nodes.name: Exhausted CD8 T cell
nodes.description: Chronic antigen drives a TOX-dependent state with high PD-1/TIM-3/LAG-3 and low effector function; TCF1+ progenitor-exhausted cells sustain the pool.
nodes.clinical_relevance: The TCF1+ progenitor-exhausted subset is the main population that expands after PD-1 blockade.

nodes.name: Hepatocyte
nodes.description: Liver parenchymal cell; IL-6–STAT3 drives the acute-phase response (CRP, fibrinogen, hepcidin).

nodes.name: Keratinocyte
nodes.description: Epidermal cell that hyperproliferates in response to IL-17 and IL-22 and produces antimicrobial peptides and chemokines.

nodes.name: Tumour cell
nodes.description: Transformed cell presenting neoantigens on MHC-I; under immune selection it loses MHC-I or upregulates PD-L1.

nodes.name: CD28
nodes.description: Constitutive T-cell co-stimulatory receptor; binding CD80/CD86 delivers signal 2 via PI3K–AKT.
nodes.clinical_relevance: TGN1412 (CD28 superagonist) caused a cytokine storm in the 2006 first-in-human study.

nodes.name: CD80/CD86 (B7)
nodes.description: Ligands on activated APCs for CD28 (activating) and CTLA-4 (inhibitory).

nodes.name: CD20
nodes.description: B-cell membrane protein expressed from pre-B to memory B cell; absent on most long-lived plasma cells.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Explains why anti-CD20 depletes B cells but pre-existing antibody titres often persist.

nodes.name: CD19
nodes.description: B-cell co-receptor expressed from pro-B cell onward, including some plasmablasts.

nodes.name: BCMA
nodes.description: B-cell maturation antigen; receptor for APRIL/BAFF that supports plasma-cell survival.

nodes.name: CD3
nodes.description: Invariant signalling chains (γδεζ) of the TCR complex bearing ITAMs.

nodes.name: MHC class I (HLA-A/B/C)
nodes.description: Presents cytosolic peptides to CD8 T cells; inhibitory ligand for NK cells.

nodes.name: MHC class II (HLA-DR/DQ/DP)
nodes.description: Presents endocytosed peptides to CD4 T cells; strongest genetic risk locus for many autoimmune diseases.
nodes.clinical_relevance: HLA-DRB1 shared epitope (RA), HLA-DQ2/DQ8 (coeliac, T1D).

nodes.name: NKG2D
nodes.description: Activating receptor on NK, CD8 and γδ T cells binding stress ligands (MICA/B, ULBPs).

nodes.name: α4β7 integrin
nodes.description: Integrin that binds MAdCAM-1 to direct lymphocytes into gut mucosa.

nodes.name: MR1
nodes.description: MHC-like molecule presenting microbial riboflavin metabolites to MAIT cells.

nodes.name: CD1d
nodes.description: Lipid-presenting MHC-like molecule recognised by iNKT cells.

nodes.name: IL-5 receptor α
nodes.description: IL-5 receptor on eosinophils and basophils.

nodes.name: Glucocorticoid receptor
nodes.description: Ligand-activated transcription factor; transrepresses NF-κB and AP-1, induces anti-inflammatory genes.

nodes.name: JAK1/JAK2
nodes.description: Janus kinases bound to cytokine receptors; phosphorylate STATs.

nodes.name: TYK2
nodes.description: JAK-family kinase transducing IL-12, IL-23 and type I IFN signals.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Loss-of-function variant P1104A protects against several autoimmune diseases.

nodes.name: Complement C5 / C5a / MAC
nodes.description: C5 cleavage releases anaphylatoxin C5a and initiates the C5b-9 membrane attack complex.

nodes.name: IgE
nodes.description: Antibody isotype that arms FcεRI on mast cells and basophils.

nodes.name: Histamine
