nodes.description: Preformed mast-cell/basophil amine causing vasodilation, permeability and bronchoconstriction.

nodes.name: Perforin / Granzyme B
nodes.description: Pore-forming protein and serine protease delivered by CTL and NK cells to induce target apoptosis.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Perforin deficiency causes familial HLH.

nodes.name: TOX
nodes.description: HMG-box transcription factor that epigenetically locks in T-cell exhaustion under chronic antigen.

nodes.name: Arginase-1 / ROS
nodes.description: MDSC-derived arginine depletion and reactive oxygen species impair TCR ζ-chain expression and T-cell proliferation.

nodes.name: IL-21
nodes.description: Tfh-derived cytokine driving germinal-centre B-cell selection and plasma-cell differentiation.

nodes.name: IL-22
nodes.description: Th17/Th22/ILC3 cytokine acting on epithelium (not immune cells) to drive barrier repair and keratinocyte proliferation.

nodes.name: IL-18
nodes.description: Inflammasome-processed cytokine that synergises with IL-12 to induce IFN-γ.

nodes.name: Gasdermin D
nodes.description: Cleaved by caspase-1 to form membrane pores that release IL-1β and execute pyroptosis.

nodes.name: Co-stimulation (signal 2)
nodes.description: CD28–CD80/86 engagement licenses naive T cells; absent signal 2 leads to anergy.

nodes.name: T-cell exhaustion programme
nodes.description: Chronic TCR stimulation → NFAT without AP-1 → TOX → inhibitory receptor expression and loss of effector function.

nodes.name: Efferocytosis & resolution
nodes.description: Clearance of apoptotic cells and lipid-mediator (resolvin) switching that actively ends inflammation.

nodes.name: Trained immunity
nodes.description: Epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming of myeloid progenitors after BCG or β-glucan that enhances later responses.

nodes.name: Class switching & somatic hypermutation
nodes.description: AID-dependent isotype switching and affinity maturation in germinal centres.
nodes.clinical_relevance: CD40L or AID deficiency → hyper-IgM syndrome.

nodes.name: Type-2 inflammation
nodes.description: Alarmin → ILC2/Th2 → IL-4/IL-5/IL-13 → IgE, eosinophilia, mucus and remodelling.

nodes.name: NETosis
nodes.description: Release of decondensed chromatin decorated with MPO/elastase; traps microbes but exposes autoantigens and drives thrombosis.

nodes.name: Acute-phase response
nodes.description: IL-6-driven hepatic production of CRP, fibrinogen, serum amyloid A and hepcidin.

nodes.name: Cancer-immunity cycle
nodes.description: Seven steps from antigen release to tumour killing (Chen & Mellman, Immunity 2013); each step is a failure point and a target.

nodes.name: Thymic selection & central tolerance
nodes.description: Positive/negative selection of thymocytes; AIRE drives self-antigen expression in thymic epithelium.
nodes.clinical_relevance: AIRE mutations → APECED/APS-1.

nodes.name: Bone marrow
nodes.description: Haematopoiesis, B-cell development and long-lived plasma-cell niches.

nodes.name: Thymus
nodes.description: Site of T-cell development and central tolerance.

nodes.name: Spleen
nodes.description: Filters blood-borne antigens; marginal-zone B cells handle encapsulated bacteria.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Asplenia → overwhelming infection with encapsulated bacteria.

nodes.name: Central nervous system
nodes.description: Microglia-dominated tissue behind the blood–brain barrier; site of MS lesions.

nodes.name: Artery wall / plaque
nodes.description: Atherosclerotic intima where lipid-laden macrophages sustain inflammation.

nodes.name: Liver
nodes.description: Kupffer cells, MAIT cells and hepatocyte acute-phase output.

nodes.name: Severe COVID-19 / ARDS
nodes.description: Late-phase hyperinflammatory lung injury in which host response, not viral load, dominates.

nodes.name: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
nodes.description: Lipid-driven arterial inflammation; residual inflammatory risk persists despite LDL lowering.

nodes.name: Multiple myeloma
nodes.description: Clonal plasma-cell neoplasm of the bone marrow.

nodes.name: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia
nodes.description: Malignancy of B-cell precursors; CD19-positive in most cases.

nodes.name: Cytokine release syndrome
nodes.description: Systemic IL-6-dominant inflammation after T-cell–engaging therapies (CAR-T, bispecifics).

nodes.name: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria
nodes.description: Acquired loss of GPI-anchored CD55/CD59 on red cells → MAC-mediated haemolysis.

nodes.name: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder
nodes.description: Anti-aquaporin-4 IgG astrocytopathy with complement-mediated optic nerve and spinal cord damage.

nodes.name: Heart failure
nodes.description: Chronic cardiac failure; relevant because high-dose anti-TNF worsened outcomes in moderate–severe disease.

nodes.name: Hyper-IgM syndrome
nodes.description: Failure of class switching (CD40L, CD40 or AID defects) → high IgM, absent IgG/IgA/IgE.

nodes.name: Gout
nodes.description: Monosodium urate crystals activate the NLRP3 inflammasome → IL-1β-driven acute arthritis.

nodes.name: Canakinumab
nodes.description: Neutralises IL-1β.
nodes.clinical_relevance: CAPS, Still disease, gout flares; tested in CANTOS.

nodes.name: Abatacept
nodes.description: Binds CD80/CD86 and blocks CD28 co-stimulation.
nodes.clinical_relevance: RA, JIA, PsA; prophylaxis of acute GVHD.

nodes.name: Ipilimumab
nodes.description: Blocks CTLA-4, enhancing priming and depleting intratumoural Tregs.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Melanoma (with nivolumab); higher rate of colitis/hypophysitis than PD-1 blockade.

nodes.name: Anakinra
nodes.description: Recombinant IL-1Ra blocking IL-1α and IL-1β signalling.

nodes.name: Eculizumab
nodes.description: Blocks C5 cleavage → no C5a or MAC.
nodes.clinical_relevance: PNH, aHUS, AQP4+ NMOSD, gMG; requires meningococcal vaccination.

nodes.name: Mepolizumab
nodes.description: Neutralises IL-5 → depletes eosinophils.
nodes.clinical_relevance: Severe eosinophilic asthma, EGPA, HES.

nodes.name: Vedolizumab
nodes.description: Gut-selective block of lymphocyte homing.

nodes.name: Colchicine
nodes.description: Disrupts microtubules → impairs neutrophil migration and NLRP3 assembly.

nodes.name: Calcineurin inhibitor
nodes.description: Blocks calcineurin → NFAT cannot enter nucleus → no IL-2.

nodes.name: TNF blockade (class)
nodes.description: Shared class effect of infliximab, adalimumab, etanercept and others.

nodes.name: Epstein–Barr virus
nodes.description: B-cell-tropic γ-herpesvirus establishing lifelong latency.

nodes.name: Neisseria meningitidis
nodes.description: Bacterium cleared primarily by complement MAC-mediated lysis.

nodes.name: Blood eosinophil count
nodes.description: Predicts response to anti-IL-5/IL-5R and dupilumab in asthma.

nodes.name: Ferritin
nodes.description: Markedly raised in HLH, macrophage activation syndrome, CRS and severe COVID-19.

nodes.name: Anti-AQP4 antibody

nodes.name: Islet autoantibodies

nodes.name: FeNO
nodes.description: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide reflects IL-13-driven airway inflammation.

nodes.name: LIBERTY ASTHMA QUEST
nodes.description: Dupilumab in uncontrolled moderate-to-severe asthma; greatest benefit with eosinophils ≥300/µL or high FeNO.

nodes.name: COLCOT

nodes.name: Lenercept in MS

nodes.name: Secukinumab in Crohn disease

nodes.name: ATTACH

nodes.name: MENSA
nodes.description: Mepolizumab reduced exacerbations in severe eosinophilic asthma.
source_refs: Ortega HG et al. N Engl J Med 2014

nodes.name: TOWER
nodes.description: Blinatumomab improved survival vs chemotherapy in relapsed/refractory B-ALL.
source_refs: Kantarjian H et al. N Engl J Med 2017

nodes.name: N-MOmentum
nodes.description: Inebilizumab reduced attacks in NMOSD.

nodes.name: GEMINI 1

nodes.name: CheckMate 067

nodes.name: BLISS-52

nodes.name: NAVIGATOR

source_refs: Menzies-Gow A et al. N Engl J Med 2021

nodes.name: POETYK PSO-1

source_refs: Armstrong AW et al. J Am Acad Dermatol 2023

relationships.mechanism: Tumour cell PD-L1 + TIL PD-1 → ZAP-70 dephosphorylation → CTL inactivation → tumour survival
relationships.consequence: Loss of T cell-mediated anti-tumour control → tumour progression

relationships.mechanism: UV-induced high somatic mutation burden in melanoma → many neoantigens → TIL-rich tumour → PD-1+ exhausted CTLs available for rescue by anti-PD-1
relationships.consequence: High TMB predicts anti-PD-1 response in melanoma; melanoma among highest TMB tumour types

relationships.mechanism: Dupilumab binds IL-4Rα → prevents IL-4 binding (Type I receptor) and IL-13 binding (Type II receptor shared with IL-13Rα1) → downstream JAK1/JAK3/STAT6 signalling blocked
relationships.consequence: Reduced Th2 differentiation, IgE class switching, goblet cell hyperplasia, FLG suppression, smooth muscle hyperresponsiveness across all type-2 target organs

relationships.mechanism: Pembrolizumab binds PD-1 on T cells → blocks PD-L1/PD-L2 interaction → restores ZAP-70 phosphorylation → rescues progenitor exhausted CTLs (TCF-1+/PD-1+/TIM-3-) from functional inactivation
relationships.consequence: CD8+ CTL reactivation → tumour cell killing; works only in progenitor exhausted state (not terminal exhaustion TOX+/TCF-1-)

relationships.mechanism: Nivolumab (anti-PD-1) blocks PD-1 on progenitor exhausted CD8 CTLs → prevents SHP-2-mediated ZAP-70 dephosphorylation → restores T cell activation capacity
relationships.consequence: Reactivated CD8 CTLs proliferate and kill tumour cells via perforin/granzyme B; durable responses when progenitor pool is maintained

relationships.mechanism: CD8+ CTLs upregulate PD-1 upon TCR activation; chronic antigen stimulation → sustained PD-1 expression → functional exhaustion
relationships.consequence: PD-1 expression marks both recently activated (good prognosis) and exhausted (requires rescue) T cells

relationships.mechanism: Tumour cells upregulate PD-L1 via: (1) oncogenic signalling (EGFR/KRAS/PI3K/MYC→STAT3→PD-L1 transcription); (2) adaptive immune resistance (TIL IFN-γ→JAK1/2→STAT1→PD-L1), tumour upregulates PD-L1 in RESPONSE to the very T cells attacking it
relationships.consequence: Blocks CTL killing via PD-1/PD-L1 interaction → acquired resistance to immune surveillance

relationships.mechanism: PD-L1 on tumour cell binds PD-1 on CTL → SHP-2 (phosphatase) recruitment to PD-1 ITSm → ZAP-70 dephosphorylation → TCR signalling disruption → T cell functional inactivation (exhaustion)
relationships.consequence: CTL cannot kill tumour cell despite antigen recognition; accumulation of exhausted TILs at tumour margin

relationships.mechanism: CTLA-4 on activated T cells/Tregs competitively outcompetes CD28 for B7 binding (higher affinity) + trans-endocytosis of B7 from APCs → reduced Signal 2 availability → T cell anergy/suppression
relationships.consequence: Peripheral tolerance maintenance; on Tregs: removes co-stimulatory capacity from APCs → suppresses effector T cell activation in vicinity

relationships.mechanism: Tregs constitutively express high levels of CTLA-4 → deplete B7 from APCs via trans-endocytosis → reduce Signal 2 availability for effector T cells (mechanism of Treg suppression)
relationships.consequence: Both normal peripheral tolerance and intratumoural Treg suppression mediated via CTLA-4; ipilimumab (IgG1) ADCC depletes CTLA-4+ Tregs in TME

relationships.mechanism: KEYnote-006: pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1) vs ipilimumab in advanced melanoma → proved PD-1 axis dominant over CTLA-4 axis as primary checkpoint in melanoma
relationships.consequence: 5yr OS 38.7% vs 31.1%; irAE 17% vs 27%; established anti-PD-1 as standard first-line for PD-L1+ advanced cancers

relationships.mechanism: IFN-α (produced by pDC after TLR7/9 activation by NETs) directly upregulates BAFF transcription in monocytes/DCs → elevated serum BAFF → autoreactive B cell rescue from apoptosis
relationships.consequence: pDC-IFN-α-BAFF chain connects innate immune hyperactivation to adaptive autoreactive B cell expansion in SLE

relationships.mechanism: Elevated BAFF provides survival signal (BAFFR/TACI/BCMA → NF-κB) to autoreactive B cells that should be eliminated by peripheral tolerance → they survive, enter GC, produce anti-dsDNA
relationships.consequence: Break in B cell peripheral tolerance → autoreactive B cell survival → GC entry → high-affinity anti-dsDNA production

relationships.mechanism: Belimumab binds free BAFF/BLyS → prevents BAFFR engagement → restores normal autoreactive B cell attrition → reduced autoantibody production
relationships.consequence: Reduced flares, lower anti-dsDNA titres, reduced complement consumption; does not reach plasma cells (CD20- and largely APRIL-dependent)

relationships.mechanism: Teplizumab (anti-CD3 Fc-silent) shifts Th1:Treg ratio in pancreatic islets → reduces insulitis intensity → slows beta-cell destruction → delays threshold crossing to clinical T1DM
relationships.consequence: T1DM onset delayed median 25 months (HR 0.41, p=0.006), first autoimmune disease delay demonstrated in humans

relationships.mechanism: TN10 trial: teplizumab vs placebo in Stage 2 T1DM → T1DM onset delayed 25 months; FDA approved as Tzield 2022; first autoimmune disease prevention drug in history
relationships.consequence: Proved Th1:Treg imbalance in islets is causally modifiable; established Stage 2 intervention as viable therapeutic window for autoimmune disease

relationships.mechanism: GC B cells undergo SHM and class switching to produce high-affinity IgG ANCA (anti-PR3 or anti-MPO) under Tfh cell help
relationships.consequence: Pathogenic ANCA IgG enters circulation and binds target antigens on primed neutrophil surface

relationships.mechanism: ANCA IgG binds PR3 or MPO antigens expressed on surface of cytokine-primed neutrophils → FcγRIII (CD16) cross-linking → neutrophil activation INSIDE vessel wall → superoxide production + degranulation → necrotising vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis
relationships.consequence: Vessel wall destruction, tissue ischaemia, glomerulonephritis (MPA/GPA), pulmonary haemorrhage

relationships.mechanism: Rituximab (anti-CD20) depletes CD20+ B cells including ANCA-producing GC B cells → ANCA IgG titres fall (to undetectable in 90% of responders in RAVE) → neutrophil FcγRIII activation reduced → vasculitis activity decreases
relationships.consequence: ANCA titres fall to undetectable in 90% of rituximab responders (RAVE pharmacodynamic proof); CR 64% vs 53% cyclophosphamide

relationships.mechanism: RAVE trial: rituximab vs cyclophosphamide in ANCA GPA/MPA → CR 64% vs 53%; ANCA undetectable 90% rituximab; superior for relapsing disease
relationships.consequence: First trial to prove B cell→ANCA→neutrophil chain causal; established rituximab as ANCA vasculitis induction standard

relationships.mechanism: B cells form leptomeningeal ectopic lymphoid follicle-like aggregates in progressive MS (compartmentalised behind closed BBB); produce pro-inflammatory cytokines, autoantibodies, and locally sustain CNS inflammation
relationships.consequence: Compartmentalised CNS B cell activity drives disability progression in PPMS (explains why T cell-targeting therapies that don't reach CNS B cells failed)

relationships.mechanism: Ocrelizumab (humanised anti-CD20) partially penetrates CNS via disrupted BBB → depletes leptomeningeal B cell aggregates in addition to peripheral B cells → slows compartmentalised CNS inflammation
relationships.consequence: 24% slower CDP in PPMS (HR 0.76, p=0.003), first positive PPMS trial; proved B cells (not T cells) are rate-limiting driver of progressive MS

relationships.mechanism: ORATORIO trial: ocrelizumab vs placebo in PPMS → first positive Phase 3 PPMS trial in history; 24% slower CDP
relationships.consequence: Proved B cells drive PPMS; established ocrelizumab as only approved PPMS therapy; changed understanding of progressive MS from T cell to B cell-driven disease

relationships.mechanism: RA synovial membrane: CD68+ macrophage density in lining layer correlates with DAS28; FLS invasion + pannus formation + RANKL-driven osteoclast activation → cartilage destruction + bone erosion; DAS28 quantifies synovial inflammation
relationships.consequence: Joint erosion (Sharp score) occurs in early untreated RA; disease modification requires treatment to DAS28 remission target

relationships.mechanism: TME composition determines whether anti-tumour immunity is operative or suppressed: hot inflamed (TIL-rich, PD-L1+, responds to anti-PD-1) vs excluded (TIL at margin, stroma barrier) vs cold (no TIL, WNT/β-catenin, no DC recruitment)
relationships.consequence: TME phenotype predicts ICI response (hot > excluded > cold); STING agonists, neoantigen vaccines target cold TME

relationships.mechanism: Gut mucosa exposed to 3.8×10^13 commensal bacteria; F. prausnitzii/Akkermansia → SCFAs (butyrate) → HDAC inhibition → Foxp3 stabilisation → Treg induction in GALT; dysbiosis → reduced Treg induction → lower tolerance threshold
relationships.consequence: Antibiotics within 30 days of ICI → reduced microbiome diversity → reduced Treg induction → shorter PFS/OS (Routy Science 2018)
